stories.title: No LPG cylinder without e-KYC in UP:Domestic consumers may have to pay double; know deadline and complete process
stories.summary: In UP, domestic gas cylinders will no longer be available without e-KYC. Nor will the subsidy come. This rule applies to both old and new customers. Ujjwala connection holders also need to get e-KYC done. No final date has been set for this yet. But if e-KYC is not done for a long time, the connection may also be blocked. The good thing is that there is no need to go to the gas agency for e-KYC. You can do e-KYC from home in a few minutes using a mobile app. How to do this, which app is needed, and what things to keep in mind? Let's find out e-KYC will be done from mobile in 5 minutes at home For e-KYC, download the official app of the gas company you are using. Indane, HP or Bharat Gas app can be found on Google Play Store. Complete the process by selecting the e-KYC option given in the app. If face authentication fails, don't panic There is no need to panic if face authentication fails. Reopen the app and repeat the face verification process. Ensure that there is sufficient light on your face and keep the mobile stable. After face scan, be sure to check the 'e-KYC Success' status in the app. Do not assume that merely by completing the face scan, e-KYC is complete. If the status does not show 'Success', then confirm the e-KYC status in your consumer record with the gas agency. 2 options for offline e-KYC If any customer is facing problems completing the process through the mobile app, then they also have other options - 1. By visiting the gas agency: You can get biometric authentication done by visiting your nearest gas agency. 2. By cylinder delivery man: When the delivery person comes home to deliver the cylinder, biometric authentication can also be done through the official device available with them. e-KYC's last date is not August 16 News reports stating August 16 as the last date for e-KYC are incorrect. Such news is circulating on social media and at the local level, but according to gas agency representatives and departmental guidelines, no final date for e-KYC has been set. The e-KYC process will continue. Both old and new customers can update their information. However, rules are in place regarding receiving cylinders without e-KYC, so customers should complete e-KYC as soon as possible. Focus on removing fake gas connections The government aims to identify and remove fake gas connections from the system. Through biometric and Aadhaar verification, it is being ensured that the subsidy money reaches the correct beneficiary and is not misused. The entire e-KYC process is completely free. Do not pay any person or agent for it. Rules related to gas cylinder delivery also changed The central government has also changed the rules related to cylinder booking. According to the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, in cities, a second cylinder can now be booked only 25 days after taking the first one. Earlier, this gap was 21 days. Whereas, in villages, the second booking can be done only after 45 days. For the delivery of a 14.2 kg domestic gas cylinder, merely showing the booking or receipt will no longer be sufficient. An OTP will be sent to the registered mobile number at the time of booking the cylinder. This OTP will have to be told to the gas agency employee at the time of delivery. The cylinder will be given only after the OTP is verified. The purpose of this is to prevent hoarding and black marketing of gas.

stories.title: Azam’s wife says, ‘They branded me as dacoit overnight’::No rules broken to build university; 'Are DM-SSP homes’ maps approved?
stories.summary: After retiring as a professor, when I started looking after the university's affairs, 60–70 cases were filed against me overnight. I was suddenly branded a thief and a dacoit. Every crime committed by criminals was linked to me. Saying this, SP leader Azam Khan's wife, Tanzim Fatima, became emotional. She said that as far as the approval of the building map was concerned, even the maps of the DM and SSP's houses were not approved. She added that Jauhar University was built before the Rampur Development Authority was established, so no rules were violated. Will Azam Khan contest the election? Tanzim Fatima says, "I have never advised Azam Sahab to leave politics." She added that Jauhar University is a greater achievement for him than politics. In an exclusive interview with Dainik Bhaskar, Tanzim Fatima also responded to questions about the allegations that Akhilesh Yadav has not fully supported Azam Khan. Read the full interview. You have received a notice to demolish 38 buildings of Jauhar University. What would you say? The Rampur Development Authority (RDA) was established in 2005. At that time, Singankheda village, where the university is located, was outside the RDA's jurisdiction. In 2015, a new notification was issued bringing Singankheda under the RDA's jurisdiction. When the university was built, the area was not under the RDA's jurisdiction. So how could the Authority have approved the building map for the area? If the court's decision goes against you, what would you consider to be the shortcoming? This is purely a political issue. Hundreds of people live in Singankheda village apart from the university, and no one's house has an approved map. Look at Rampur or other cities, even the official residences of the DM and SP do not have approved maps. If the administration takes action, it will be seen as an attempt to destroy an educational institution. Dozens of cases have been registered against your family. How do you view this? This is purely political vendetta. Before entering politics, I was a professor at a degree college. No one questioned my honesty until I retired. But after retirement, when I took over the university's affairs, 60–70 cases were registered against me. Overnight, I became a thief and a dacoit. It is alleged that Akhilesh Yadav did not fully support Azam Khan. Is that true? No, this is incorrect. Akhilesh Yadav and the entire SP have stood by us. The party has provided us with full support in every way. Shivpal Singh Yadav himself went to meet Azam Sahab in jail and also held a press conference. Mulayam Singh Yadav also made a major contribution to the construction of this university. If the administration considers a police camp necessary on the university campus for security, what will you do? Around two or three years ago, the police entered the campus without permission. They neither sought permission from the Vice-Chancellor nor from anyone else. The police ransacked our rooms and records and took away whatever items they wanted. At the time, we approached the High Court. The court ordered that the police could not enter the campus without permission. If there is a police camp on every university campus, then we have no objection. Many obstacles arose during the construction of the university. How much cooperation did local people provide? Yes, it was a test because some people continuously created problems. But local people provided a great deal of support in building the university. Children and students from Rampur worked here themselves. They helped construct the university by carrying bricks, stones, cement and soil on their heads in the scorching heat. Is children's education being affected by the action taken against the university? Yes, education is definitely being affected. There are many expensive schools in Rampur where the fees are very high. People from poorer sections of society cannot afford such fees. Azam Sahab established Rampur Public Schools keeping in mind the poverty, illiteracy and economic condition of the people of Rampur. At present, an RPS school is operating, although its building is under a stay order, and some children are studying there. The fees can be compared with those of other schools. This will show how beneficial these schools were for children from poor families. What is Azam Khan's biggest achievement — politics or Jauhar University? Certainly, Jauhar University is his biggest achievement. Rampur was a very backward district in terms of education. While serving as an MLA and MP 10 times, Azam Sahab gave priority to education alongside development. He opened Rampur Public Schools for orphaned children from poor and labouring families, where CBSE education was provided for just ₹20 a month. The government had those schools vacated, which harmed the orphaned children. Will Azam Khan contest elections again or distance himself from politics? Whether Azam Sahab will contest elections again or not, only time will tell. At present, our effort is to secure his release from jail. I have never advised him to leave politics. However, politics 20–25 years ago was not like it is today. Back then, during Eid and Bakrid, leaders of opposition parties and government officials would visit each other's homes. That era is now gradually disappearing from politics. Stay on demolition of 38 university buildings maintained A hearing was held on August 13 in the Commissioner's Court in Moradabad against the order to demolish 38 buildings of Jauhar University. After the hearing, the court of Divisional Commissioner Anjaneya Kumar Singh upheld the interim stay imposed on July 27 against the Rampur DM's demolition order.

stories.title: Ganga changes course, school submerged in Badaun:Villagers say they had to relocate 2–4 km after every flood; now no land is left
stories.summary: The rising Ganga river in Badaun is becoming dangerous. In just five minutes, strong currents engulf the entire government school building in Kadmanagla village, leaving only a few walls. Students have been transferred to a primary school in another village, but families trapped by the flood are unable to send their children to school. Standing crops across around 1,000 bighas are submerged after the Ganga changes course. Villagers move to safer places as their homes and fields go underwater. Villagers say the river is rapidly eroding the land, and this is not the first time. The village has been washed away and merged into the river three times before. Residents rebuilt their homes in fields after moving away from the river, but there is now not enough farmland to accommodate so many families. This time, the village itself is on the verge of disappearing. People in panic, did not put roofs on their houses Kadmanagla village is about 40 km from Badaun district headquarters. Nearby are several villages including Raipura, Damnagla, and Jata. Currently, all these villages are in the grip of floods and erosion. There is no paved road left to reach these villages. People are commuting through unpaved and pothole-filled roads. Even these are filled with 1 to 2 feet of water. There are about 100 houses in villages like Kadmanagla, Damnagla, and Raipura, none of which are two-storied. Most people haven't even put roofs on their houses. When asked the reason, they say, There is always a fear that the flood in the Ganga might wash away our houses at any time. That's why we have only built enough to shelter our heads. Village washed away twice We met Ram Singh in Kadmanagla village. He says their earlier settlement, Kheda Pukhta, was submerged in a Ganga flood in 1965. The river receded after eroding the land but changed its course, forcing villagers to settle on the other side, where they named the village Kadmanagla. They lived there for 10 years before another flood reached their homes and eroded the land again. The villagers then moved to their own fields, where they have lived for around 20 years. Now, the Ganga has changed its course for the third time, flooding the entire village and rapidly eroding the land. The strong current has once again left residents frightened. 'Grandfather, father and we saw floods, now we won't let our children suffer this' Villager Ram Singh says, Until now, we kept moving towards our fields, but now behind us are the villages of Farrukhabad, our field has also been cut, now we don't understand where to go? My grandfather, father, and we have seen the crisis of floods, now we don't want our children to suffer it, we just want them to go anywhere and work as laborers, but leave this place. ‘This is all Ganga’s grace’ Ninety-year-old Kripal Singh Yadav, the oldest resident of the village, says, ‘This is all the grace of Mother Ganga.’ When asked how he could call it a blessing after losing both his home and farmland to erosion, he says, ‘What else can I say? What is destined is happening.’ He says villagers have no basic facilities and are somehow making a living. Government officials visit, inspect the situation and leave. With their farmland disappearing, many residents have also started going out to work as labourers. 'We just think that if a dam is built, then the lands will be saved' 38-year-old Amit Yadav's house is currently just 100 meters away from the river. He says that we studied outside, kept looking for a job, when we didn't get a job, we came back here. After all, even if we leave, where would we go? Regarding the future, we only think that if the government builds a dam here, and our fields are saved, then our situation will improve. Flooded school shifts 41 students The Upper Primary School in Kadamanagla village is now submerged in the Ganga. Its 41 students are shifted to Damangala Primary School, 2 km away, which already has 43 students and two teachers. The same teachers now teach students from Classes 6 to 8. The school is also affected by flooding, with only around 20 children attending. Teacher Dilshad Hussain says Kadamanagla had no permanent teacher even earlier, with a teacher from another school assigned there. After the school collapses, the remaining students are taught by him and the principal. Only 2–3 children from Kadamanagla attend because of the flood, and teachers sometimes drop them home on bikes. Dilshad says he was earlier posted in Sonbhadra, where even village roads were paved, but Kadamanagla has no proper roads. After explaining the situation, he rides through 3 feet of floodwater on his bike towards the nearest town, with the bike barely able to move. 'Officials came, but no one did anything' Village head Rakesh Kashyap says, Hundreds of bighas of land in our village have been submerged in the river this year. Now, 10 to 15 meters of land are eroding and submerging into the river every day. There are currently about 25 houses in the village. All are under threat. The SDM came twice, and officials from the flood division also came. They also said that if the water level decreases, we will consider building a dam. Jitendra, standing next to the head, says, Officials do come, but they look and then leave. It would be very good if there was a system to stop the erosion. We don't have jobs, if the land is saved, we will be able to feed our children.

stories.title: Bride flees on fifth day of marriage:Runs off with ₹11 lakh in jewellery and cash; middleman threatens to frame groom’s family in case
stories.summary: A bride fled from her in-laws’ house in Agra just five days after the wedding, taking jewellery and cash worth ₹11 lakh with her. The husband and his family contacted the matchmaker, hoping he might know where she had gone. However, the family alleges that instead of helping them, the middleman threatened to implicate them in a case for allegedly making the woman disappear. According to the family, matchmaker had portrayed the woman as being from a financially weak background and persuaded them to agree to the marriage, saying it would help her build a better life. After the bride disappeared, the husband and his family approached the police to lodge a complaint, but alleged that their complaint was not initially accepted. An FIR has now been registered following a court order. Now, complete matter in detail Guddi Devi, a resident of Awas Vikas Colony Sector-14 in Agra, said that I have three sons. My youngest son Rahul is already married. The search for a match for my eldest son Vishnu's marriage was ongoing. The elder son does flower decoration work. She was looking for a girl for his marriage. She met Jawahar Singh, a resident of Shamsabad. He told her - There is a poor girl named Preeti who lives in Prayagraj. She doesn't have a father. I know her brother. You just have to bear the expenses from both sides. She agreed to the marriage after being convinced by his words. Wedding took place on 27th June Guddi Devi alleges that the young woman's brother, Dhara Singh, demanded ₹1.5 lakh in the name of buying wedding items. The family transferred ₹1 lakh in cash and ₹50,500 online. On 27th June 2026, the wedding rituals were completed at the woman's house, and Preeti started living in the house as a daughter-in-law. Bride suddenly disappeared after 5 days 5 days after the wedding, on the morning of 3rd July, the mother-in-law called her daughter-in-law Preeti for tea. But she was found missing from the house. Guddi Devi said that she searched for her daughter-in-law everywhere. But nothing was found. When checked at home, 4 tolas of gold and 1 kg of silver jewelry were missing. These include two mangalsutras, three gold rings, a silver waistband, and anklets. She also stole ₹16,000 from the ‘Muh dikhai’ ceremony and the younger daughter-in-law's gold ring, mangalsutra, payal, and ₹15,000. The matchmaker Jawahar, said on the phone that you people should not complain to the police. I will bring the girl back. For many days, there was no response from him. Then, he started threatening that he would implicate them in a case of making the girl disappear. After this, the family went to Sikandra police station to file a complaint, but said that the police did not hear their case. An FIR was eventually registered following a court order. DCP City Syed Ali Abbas said, “Action is being taken based on the evidence. Efforts are underway to trace the bride, who is accused of theft. The matchmaker who arranged the marriage is also being traced.”

stories.title: Yogi tells athletes, 'Win medals, we’ll give jobs':Those who chant 'youth-youth' have no agenda for youth, only mafias
stories.summary: CM Yogi Adityanath arrived at Gorakhnath Temple to watch the wrestling competition organized on the occasion of Nag Panchami in Gorakhpur on Monday afternoon at 3 PM. CM Yogi told the players that we are directly giving jobs to those who win medals for the country. So far, 500 players have been given jobs. The CM said- Today some people are shouting youth-youth, but youth is not in their agenda. They just want to use you. When they were in power, they did nothing for the youth and handed everything over to the mafia. Before this, CM Yogi performed worship of Guru Gorakhnath at Gorakhnath Temple. He went to the samadhi site of Brahmaleen Mahant Avaidyanath and took his blessings. After this, he watched the wrestling matches of the wrestlers. He honored the winning wrestlers. In the presence of the CM, the title matches of Uttar Pradesh Kesari, Uttar Pradesh Kumar and Uttar Pradesh Veer Abhimanyu were held. More than 300 wrestlers participated in this two-day state-level competition. See 2 pictures CM said- If you engage in sports, you will stay away from drugs CM Yogi said that the more youth engage with sports, the more they will stay away from addiction. There are two forms of addiction. One is drugs and intoxicating substances, while the other is smartphone addiction. Today, 90% of the time youth spend on smartphones is wasted. If even one hour from the time spent on smartphones is dedicated to the body, then the body will remain healthy. If the body is healthy, then the mind will also remain healthy. This will enable youth to contribute to making the nation stronger. The first rule for an athlete is self-discipline. They wake up and sleep on time. They follow dietary rules. Old coaches prepared athletes by tempering their lives even with limited resources and without incentives. Today, all kinds of facilities are available for athletes. Government will also help private sports academies; new youth policy soon The CM said that the UP government is soon bringing a new youth policy. Under this, many events and programs will be started for the youth. 'Abhyudaya Coaching' for youth preparing for competitive exams will be extended to every college and university. This facility will be available through both physical and virtual mediums. A 'Skilling and Employment Zone' is being created in every district of the state. Here, under one roof, along with skilling of youth, employment facilities will also be available. If the private sector cooperates in any field of sports, then full support will be provided to it under the state government's sports policy. Strictness against those who play with the future of youth Yogi said that if the copying mafia or education mafia plays with the future of any youth, strict action will be taken against them. Action is also being taken to confiscate the property of such people. He mentioned the sports talents of Ghazipur, saying that Olympic medal winners Lalit Upadhyay and Rajkumar Pal have progressed from Ghazipur's private stadium. He said that this shows that better sports facilities and private academies can play a crucial role in advancing youth. Education, sports and protecting youth from drug mafia is necessary The CM said that old players, wrestlers and coaches dedicated their lives to sports with limited resources and without encouragement. If they had received adequate facilities and encouragement at that time, they could have taken the country's name even further at the international level. He said that sports and youth were not on the agenda of previous governments. Today some people are shouting youth-youth, but while in power they did nothing for the welfare of youth. They handed over the youth power to the mafia. 'Mafia mentality is the biggest enemy of youth power' CM Yogi said that mafia mentality is the biggest enemy of youth power. Whether it is education mafia, sports mafia, drug mafia, or professional criminals, youth suffer the most because of this. To protect youth from this, it is necessary to promote sports and sports culture. The double engine government under the leadership of PM Narendra Modi is working to create a positive environment for sports and youth. He said that a wrestler follows discipline and a sattvic lifestyle. He is also a devotee of Bajrangbali, from whom strength, intelligence, and knowledge are sought..

stories.title: Woman cop who arrested Muskan in 'blue drum case' suspended:Shared videos promoting QR code, was posted at Meerut SSP office
stories.summary: The female inspector who arrested Muskan, accused of dismembering her husband in Meerut, has been suspended. A video related to the officer surfaced on social media on Sunday, following which action was taken against her. The officer, Anu, is originally from Prayagraj and belongs to the 2023 batch of Sub-Inspectors. At the time of the Blue drum case, she was posted at Brahmpuri police station. She was later transferred to the SSP’s office. Anu’s first posting in Meerut was at Rohta police station. Pictures related to the female inspector on social media... YouTuber complained about inspector Anu, says, Yogiji, please A YouTuber had complained about female inspector Anu's objectionable posts on social media. He also released a video to make his point. In which he says- Yogi ji, namaste. Yaar, you can say whatever you want; you are the cutest person. Yogi ji is my most favorite Prime Minister. I mean, it came out wrong from my mouth, but you think about it, I'm going in the right direction, right? Not 29, so what, 34. You'll have my full support, sir. Sir, I wanted to show you a video. Look at this video. I know, Yogi ji, it's the wrong video, and you have a right to be angry. You basically don't pay any attention at all to all these things. This video is of Annie Collis, who is a Sub Inspector in the Uttar Pradesh Police. She has Instagram and YouTube channels. She posts reels on them. Some objectionable videos also appear on the YouTube channel. A QR code is also visible along with it. Basically, for donations. You understand the purpose, don't you? This uniform of Uttar Pradesh- if something could be done about its dignity. Now, our DGP sahab, Rajeev Krishna ji. I mean, our country's most important state. One of the most important states is Uttar Pradesh, and its police. If someone sees it, sir. I'm saying, if Haryana police see that, brother, QR codes of Uttar Pradesh police are running at night. I mean, they make a lot of fun on WhatsApp groups internally. You have rules and regulations, right? Steps should be taken against them. There is power; I mean, I don't have it, that's why I allow everything. Do it on Instagram, do it on YouTube too. Just what happens is that the dignity of the uniform falls a little. Yogi ji, Rajiv Krishna ji, let me tell you one thing. Just issue a simple circular, a notification, that police personnel or bureaucrats who are in high positions, who are in good important, significant positions. They should not be allowed to do such dramas on social media or do all this on social media. It looks wrong. It's disrespectful. Whether you believe it or not, dignity falls. Respect falls. Otherwise, great Yogi ji. Big fan. Anu's Instagram account is named Ani Colliss Anu has an account on Instagram with the name Annie Collis. It has 684 posts and 1,016 followers. Sub Inspector Uttar Pradesh Police is written in the profile. It also says, ‘Age Grace My Love’. A YouTube channel link is also attached below. Arrested Muskan in the Blue Drum Saurabh Murder Case Anu is the same woman police officer who arrested and brought accused Muskan in the 2025 Blue Drum murder case. At that time, Anu was posted at Brahmpuri police station. During this time, the famous blue drum case came to light. Anu had also shared a video with Muskan on her social media account. In this video, she can be seen with Muskan. Police will investigate lady inspector's video Action was taken against lady inspector Anu after reports emerged of a violation of the police department's social media policy. Its departmental inquiry has been assigned to CO office officer Saumya Singh. The police will now investigate the reality check of inspector Anu's video along with its source. The team will also find out whether any kind of tampering was done with the lady inspector's video that surfaced on social media. Besides this, facts related to inspector Anu's social media activities will also be investigated. SP Crime Meerut Avneesh Kumar said that in the case of woman sub-inspector Anu, along with a departmental inquiry, an investigation is also being conducted at the cyber level. After the investigation report comes, necessary departmental action will be taken based on the facts. The conduct of the woman sub-inspector falls under the category of violation of the department's social media policy. Such video-related activities while holding a post are wrong. She has been suspended on this basis. The woman sub-inspector's Instagram and YouTube channels are also being investigated. Objectionable videos related to social media have been removed. The woman sub-inspector's account has also been deleted.

stories.title: ATS arrests Jaish-e-Mohammed terrorist from mosque in Meerut:24-yr-old considered Masood his mentor; made masked videos urging people to wage jihad
stories.summary: UP Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) has arrested Mohammad Zafar, a suspected terrorist linked to the Pakistani terrorist organization Jaish-e-Mohammed. This arrest was made on Sunday from a mosque in Meerut. 24-year-old Zafar is a resident of Purnia district in Bihar. He obtained a Maulvi degree from a madrasa in Meerut in 2022. He had come to Meerut just two months ago. ATS issued a press note on Monday. The allegation is that he was collecting donations from people in the name of the madrasa and sending that money to the terrorist organization Jaish-e-Mohammed in Pakistan. During the investigation, evidence of Pakistani jihadi WhatsApp groups and activities related to jihad-caliphate on social media were found on his mobile. During interrogation, Zafar revealed that during his studies he had read about Jaish-e-Mohammed. He was influenced by reading about jihad and the martyrdom of Mujahideen. Coming under the influence of Maulana Masood Azhar, he wanted to become a mujahid. Was influenced by Masood Azhar's speeches According to ATS, Zafar was influenced by the speeches of Jaish-e-Mohammed chief Masood Azhar. He used to share his inflammatory and jihadi speeches to incite people for violent jihad. During the investigation, such activities were found on his social media accounts. On Facebook, he used to post statements related to jihad and caliphate with his face covered. The Pakistani jihadi WhatsApp groups found on Zafar's mobile contained discussions about jihad and donations. Zafar joined this jihadi group of Jaish-e-Mohammed and came in contact with a Pakistani handler. He had also offered to help the handler in jihad. Money sent through binance account According to ATS, Zafar attempted to send money at the behest of a Pakistani handler. After this, he requested information about a Binance account. The suspect remained in contact with Pakistani individuals and sent money multiple times through cryptocurrency USDT. The investigating agency is now gathering information about his contacts, transactions, and other people connected to the terrorist network. ATS has registered an FIR against Zafar. The investigating agency is examining his social media accounts, chats found on his mobile, and contacts linked to Pakistan. Additionally, it is also being investigated where the money was sent through donations and cryptocurrency. Who else besides Zafar is involved in this network? Terrorist Masood Azhar formed JeM 26 years ago Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) is a terrorist organization of Pakistan. It was formed by terrorist Masood Azhar in the year 2000. It is accused of carrying out terrorist attacks in several countries, including India. Jaish's headquarters is in Bahawalpur in Punjab province of Pakistan. This organization operates training camps and terrorist networks in several areas of Pakistan. Its chief terrorist, Masood Azhar, was arrested in Jammu and Kashmir in the year 1994. However, after the hijacking of Indian Airlines flight IC-814 in December 1999, the Government of India released him in exchange for the release of hostages.

stories.title: 8 UP faces, including two Muslims, in BJP’s new team:Three women given key roles; Harish Dwivedi and Basit Ali get promotions
stories.summary: BJP national president Nitin Nabin announced his new team at 3 pm on Monday. Six leaders from Uttar Pradesh have been included in the national team, while the presidents of the OBC and Minority Morchas are also from UP. This takes the total number of UP leaders in Nabin’s team to eight. The BJP has formed the team with next year’s Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in mind. UP has the highest representation of women in the national team among all states, with three leaders: Smriti Irani, Rekha Verma and Sangeeta Yadav. Two leaders from the Pasmanda Muslim community have also been given positions in the national organisation. They include former Aligarh Muslim University Vice-Chancellor Dr. Tariq Mansoor and National Minority Morcha president Kunwar Basit Ali. Mansoor has been reappointed as national vice-president, while Basit Ali has been promoted from his current position as president of the UP BJP Minority Morcha. In terms of caste representation, the team includes one Brahmin, one Parsi, one SC leader and three OBC leaders from the Yadav, Kurmi and Maurya communities. The formation of the team had been pending since Nabin took over as BJP national president seven months ago. Who is close to whom? Find out… Smriti Irani: She is considered one of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s close leaders and was a key BJP face against Rahul Gandhi in Amethi. Harish Dwivedi: A former MP from Basti, he is considered close to Home Minister Amit Shah, JP Nadda, and the RSS. He is also regarded as one of the central leadership’s trusted leaders. Rekha Verma: She is considered close to the central leadership and has been reappointed as national vice-president. This is being seen as a sign of her acceptability within the organisation. She is not associated with any particular faction. Tariq Mansoor: He is one of the key figures in the Modi-BJP’s Muslim outreach strategy. As a former AMU vice-chancellor, he has been given another opportunity to help the BJP connect with the Muslim community, particularly the Pasmanda section. Bhola Singh: His inclusion is linked to the party’s central organisation and Dalit strategy. He has been elected MP from Bulandshahr three consecutive times and has worked at the national level in the SC Morcha. His political role is primarily linked to Dalit representation. Sangeeta Yadav: Her husband is an IRS officer. She has stayed away from factional politics and is expected to be useful to the party’s social engineering strategy as both a woman and a Yadav face. Sangeeta Yadav has served as a BJP national secretary. She was an MLA from Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur and is now a Rajya Sabha MP. Amar Pal Maurya: He is considered close to Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya and has also worked with Uma Bharti. Kunwar Basit Ali: He has been associated with the RSS-linked Muslim Rashtriya Manch and has been a prominent face of the BJP’s Muslim outreach campaign. He is considered one of Amit Shah’s trusted leaders. Regional equations were also taken into account Sangeeta Yadav, Harish Dwivedi and Amar Pal Maurya have been given representation from eastern UP. From western UP, Prof Tariq Mansoor, Kunwar Basit Ali and Bhola Singh have been included in the organisation. Rekha Verma from Rohilkhand and Smriti Irani from central UP have also been given positions, ensuring representation across the state. 4 leaders dropped from the organisation Why were UP leaders given importance? Uttar Pradesh is one of the BJP’s most important states, with the 2027 Assembly elections approaching. With 403 Assembly seats, UP has the largest legislative assembly in the country. It also sends 80 MPs to the Lok Sabha. The presence of UP leaders in the BJP’s national organisation could therefore have a direct bearing on the party’s strategy for the upcoming Assembly elections. Regional and social equations are also believed to have influenced the decision to give key responsibilities to leaders from UP. The reappointment of Harish Dwivedi and Rekha Verma to important positions is being seen as an effort to balance the party’s organisational experience with its electoral requirements. UP has highest representation with 3 women in Nitin Nabin’s team BJP president Nitin Nabin’s new national team has given responsibilities to 12 women. They include General Secretary Smriti Irani, Vice-President Rekha Verma and National Secretary Sangeeta Yadav. With three women, Uttar Pradesh has the highest representation in the team. Maharashtra has two women, while the remaining states have one woman each. Nitin became BJP president 209 days ago Nitin Nabin became the BJP’s national president 209 days ago, replacing JP Nadda. He was elected unopposed and, at 45, became the BJP’s youngest-ever national president.

stories.title: Ram Mandir donation theft:SIT report cannot be shared with outsiders, Solicitor General tells SC; court asks for sealed copy
stories.summary: The Ayodhya Ram Mandir donation theft case was heard in the Supreme Court on Monday afternoon. The petitioners’ lawyers asked the court to provide them with the investigation report so they could assist in the proceedings. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta opposed the request, saying the report could not be shared with people who were not directly connected with the case. The petitioners’ lawyer responded that they were not strangers and that the plea had been filed on behalf of the people of India. The lawyer argued that they had a fundamental right to know the truth. He said that if investigation-related information had been shared with an accused or someone assisting the probe while the petitioners were kept out, they would not be able to effectively assist the court. On this, the Supreme Court made a stern remark saying - We have constituted the SIT. It is answerable and accountable to the court. It has to submit its report to us only. The SIT with a forensic auditor should file its status report in a sealed cover in the Supreme Court. We will see the report first. After that, we will decide whether to hand it over to all parties or not. The bench of Chief Justice (CJI) Suryakant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing petitions demanding a CBI investigation into the theft of offerings. Earlier, on 27 July, the court had directed the inclusion of a forensic auditor in the SIT to examine accounts and records to detect financial irregularities. On 20 July, the court had ordered the UP government to constitute a fresh Special Investigation Team (SIT). Court room LIVE Supreme Court: The petitioner or any other well-intentioned person with a public-interest spirit can give their suggestions to the Solicitor General's office. These suggestions can be about aspects that need thorough investigation by the SIT. Petitioner's Lawyer: We should be given a copy of the investigation report so that we can assist the court. Solicitor General: The investigation report cannot be shared with any unknown person or external party. Petitioner's Lawyer: We are not unknown. This petition has been filed on behalf of the people of India. We have a fundamental right to know the truth. Petitioner's Lawyer: I would like to place one matter before you. This case is pending before this court, and the Chief Minister is publicly citing the SIT (Special Investigation Team) findings and saying that no sadhu is involved in this. Chief Justice: If the SIT is doing its work satisfactorily, then that is a different matter. But, if you feel that there is some deficiency in their work and it needs improvement, then our stance is open. We can issue new guidelines. Earlier, Vijay Vishwas Pant's SIT had conducted the investigation

stories.title: Three children drown in pond:Tragedy strikes 100 metres from home during Nag Panchami bath
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, on Nag Panchami, three children drowned while bathing in a pond about 100 metres away from their home. Villagers pulled all three out of the pond. They were taken to the hospital, where doctors declared all three dead after examination. The ages of the three were 9, 12, and 14 years. Police have sent the children's bodies for post-mortem. The incident occurred at 10 AM on Monday in Badauli Babu, Bansgaon, about 25 kilometers from the district headquarters. Upon receiving information, police and administrative officials, including MLA Dr. Vimlesh Paswan, reached the spot. 2 pictures related to the accident Children from the village had gathered by the pond in Badouli Babu village on Nagpanchami. Meanwhile, some children started bathing. Three children went into deep water and started drowning. Seeing the children drowning, some children who were already bathing somehow got out and informed the villagers upon reaching the village. Vikas Singh, the representative of the village head from the village, gathered some people and reached the pond. He immediately started rescue operations with the villagers. The children were searched for in the pond using fishing nets. After much effort, one child was pulled out, but he had already died on the spot. Subsequently, two other children were also pulled out and immediately sent to the hospital, where doctors also declared both of them dead. As soon as the news of the incident spread, a large number of villagers gathered near the pond. The family members are distraught with grief. A wave of mourning has swept across the entire village due to this accident. These three children died MLA and officials assured help Upon receiving information about the accident, Bansgaon MLA Dr. Vimlesh Paswan, Tehsildar Bansgaon, Block Head Representative Shivaji Singh, and Block Head Shivaji Chand, along with several public representatives and officials, reached the spot. They gathered information about the incident and met the victim families, assuring them of help.

stories.title: SP and BJP leaders clash in wrestling bout:15-minute match in Varanasi ends in draw; had also contested election against each other
stories.summary: A unique contest took place in a Varanasi wrestling arena on Nag Panchami. SP leader Aman Yadav and BJP councillor Ram Singh Kallu, who had previously faced each other in an electoral contest, went head-to-head in the wrestling arena on Monday. Their bout at the Bachau Veer Akhara at BHU lasted around 15 minutes. Both tried several moves to pin each other down, but neither could secure a victory. The match ended in a draw, with the ₹5,100 prize money divided equally between them. See pictures- Wrestlers gather at Kashi akharas Wrestling in Kashi's akharas is part of a long-standing Nag Panchami tradition. Wrestlers began arriving at different arenas from around 7am on Monday. Children and adults alike took part at the Bachau Veer Akhara, located at the ancient Hanuman temple on the BHU campus. Ram Singh Kallu and Aman Yadav also train at this akhara. When someone invited the two leaders to wrestle against each other, they entered the arena and tested their strength. The crowd's enthusiasm grew as soon as the bout began. For around 15 minutes, both wrestlers attempted to pin each other, but neither managed to win. The referee ultimately declared both of them winners, and the ₹5,100 prize money was shared equally. The two had also competed against each other in the last councillor election from the same ward. The SP fielded Aman Yadav, while the BJP nominated Ram Singh Kallu. Ram Singh won that electoral contest. Dutch visitor swings 21kg mace At 9am, the Hanuman idol was formally worshipped at the historic akhara at Tulsi Ghat. The wrestlers then bowed to the soil before beginning their bouts. Local residents and visitors from outside the city gathered to watch. Herbert, a visitor from the Netherlands, also attended the akhara. He watched the wrestlers, learnt about Indian wrestling techniques and observed traditional exercises. He swung a 21kg mace and also learnt how the jori, a pair of heavy clubs, is used. Herbert said he first visited India in 2017. Since then, he has developed an interest in traditional Indian sports and akhara culture and now also trains wrestlers in the Netherlands. Wants to train in the rain Herbert said traditional Indian exercises are not merely about physical strength but are rooted in a long-standing sporting and training tradition. He particularly enjoys practising with the jori and swinging the mace. Despite the rain during the wrestling programme, he expressed his desire to train in the akhara and said he would practise there if the rain stopped. Gullu and Kashi Pehlwan also draw Another bout at the Bachau Veer Akhara saw Gullu Pehlwan take on Kashi Pehlwan. Their match also ended in a draw. A large number of local wrestlers took part in the Nag Panchami competition, continuing Kashi's traditional akhara wrestling culture. Performances help identify weaknesses Vishambhar Nath Mishra, who runs the akhara and is a professor at BHU-IIT, said the annual Nag Panchami programme was organised at the venue. He said the day's rituals and worship were performed, with the Hanuman idol brought from Sankat Mochan Temple for worship. Performances were then organised for the boys and girls training at the akhara. According to Mishra, the purpose of these performances is to identify where each trainee is weaker or stronger so that their shortcomings can be corrected and they can be trained accordingly.

stories.title: IPS Ashutosh Mishra’s mother’s death case takes a turn:SP says no injury marks on body, son files murder FIR
stories.summary: The case of the death of Indravati, mother of IPS Ashutosh Mishra, in Ambedkar Nagar is getting complicated. No injury marks were found on her body in the post-mortem report. However, to know the clear cause of death, the viscera will be preserved and sent to the forensic lab. Histopathological examination of the heart will also be conducted. IPS Ashutosh Mishra has expressed apprehension of murder after robbery, stating that gold jewelry was missing from his mother's body. He has registered a case of murder and robbery against unknown persons. Meanwhile, SP Prachi Singh informed that IPS's uncle Ramesh Chandra Mishra had informed the police station about Indravati's death due to a heart attack. The case is from Rudha Dhamrua village, 30 kilometers away from the district headquarters. 91-year-old Indravati Devi was found dead at home. Ashutosh Mishra apprehended that thieves who entered the house murdered her after robbing her. Meanwhile, on Monday morning, Indravati's bier was decorated amidst a somber atmosphere in the village. Family members and relatives left for Ayodhya with the body. Her last rites will be performed here at Saryu Ghat. View photos Know the full story IPS Ashutosh Mishra, a resident of Rudha Dhamarua village, is the only son of his parents. His two sisters are married. His father, Ramkumar Mishra, was a principal at a government inter college. He passed away about a year and a half ago. After this, Indravati was living alone at home. To care for his mother, Ashutosh had hired a maid named Piyari. He himself also used to visit the village with his family from time to time. When the maid arrived at the house in the morning to clean, Indravati was lying on the cot. She thought she was sleeping. There was no movement when she called out. When she went closer, Indravati was found dead. The maid informed Ashutosh's uncle, Ramesh Chandra Mishra alias Kallu, who lived nearby. After this, the uncle called Ashutosh and informed him about his mother's death. He described it as a death due to heart attack and asked him to come to the village soon. Jewellery found missing upon IPS's arrival Ashutosh reached the village and inquired about the incident from the maid and uncle. After observing the condition of the body, it was found that Indravati's gold chain and Tulsi necklace from her neck, nose pin, and ear tops were missing. The anklets worn on her feet were also not found. Following this, he registered a case of murder after robbery against an unknown person. Upon receiving information about the incident, Ayodhya Range DIG Somen Verma and SP Prachi Singh reached the spot. The police team meticulously inspected the crime scene. No injury marks in post-mortem According to the police, no injury marks were found on Indravati's body. There was blood on her lips. Family members stated that she was a patient of high blood pressure. A panel of three doctors conducted the post-mortem with videography. No clear facts confirming murder emerged from it. To ascertain the actual cause of death, the viscera has been sent to the forensic lab. Heart will also be examined Histopathological examination of the deceased's heart will also be conducted. This will help in determining the cause of death. Police are also investigating whether the death was actually due to cardiac reasons or if there was another cause behind it. SP Prachi said Currently, the post-mortem has not revealed any facts that would prima facie confirm murder. Considering the apprehension expressed by the family members and the disappearance of jewelry, the police are investigating all aspects. The cause of death will become clearer after the scientific examination report of the viscera and heart is received.

stories.title: ‘Used to get irritated hearing about ration dealers’:CM Yogi raise commission to ₹125 per quintal, promises additional increase by ₹25
stories.summary: The Yogi government has increased the commission paid to ration dealers in Uttar Pradesh by ₹35 per quintal. The commission has risen from ₹90 to ₹125 per quintal, benefiting more than 78,000 ration dealers across the state. Speaking at an event at Lok Bhavan, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said ration dealers were viewed with suspicion before 2017 and did not receive the respect they deserved. He said corruption in the system was committed by others, but ration dealers often faced the consequences. Ration shops to become Annapurna centres Yogi said ration shops are being developed as Annapurna centres, with ₹500 crore being allocated for the initiative. The centres will have both shops and warehouses. Earlier, dealers could sell only ration, but they will now be allowed to sell 39 types of items. The Chief Minister said the state government has also written to the Centre seeking another ₹25-per-quintal increase. If approved, the commission will rise to ₹150 per quintal. A new e-POS feedback system has also been launched, allowing dealers to send their views on ration supply and distribution directly to the government digitally. Monthly earnings to rise Yogi said ration dealers continued distributing foodgrains during the COVID-19 pandemic, including under schemes providing pulses, salt and cooking oil, without complaints about access. According to him, a dealer distributing around 100 quintals a month previously earned about ₹12,750, while the revised arrangement will raise this to ₹16,250. This represents an increase in the margin, while dealers can also earn additional profits from selling other products. He said around 15 crore people in Uttar Pradesh currently receive free ration, compared with the situation before 2017, when ration cards were allegedly misused and deaths from hunger were reported. Yogi highlights changes in education and foodgrain procurement Yogi said the government had improved basic education infrastructure through Operation Kayakalp, including flooring, drinking water, smart classrooms and furniture. Around 1.60 crore children are being provided bags, books, uniforms, shoes, socks and sweaters. He also claimed that before 2017 many schools lacked buildings and teachers, while in some cases teachers were present but students were not. On foodgrain procurement, Yogi alleged that widespread irregularities previously prevented farmers from receiving the benefit of the Minimum Support Price. He said the government now purchases directly from farmers and transfers payments to their bank accounts through DBT. He also warned that money flowing abroad through illicit channels could be used to fund terrorism. Keshav Maurya targets opposition ahead of 2027 polls Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya said the BJP government had followed the principle of serving both those who voted for it and those who did not. Referring to the 2027 Assembly elections, he said the Election Commission could announce the polls in early 2027, although he did not know the exact timing. He questioned the opposition's contribution to the construction of the Ram temple and criticised the Samajwadi Party's previous government. Maurya said Uttar Pradesh had undergone significant change and asked those present to raise their hands in support of the BJP in 2027. He remarked that those who did not raise their hands would be assumed to support the Samajwadi Party. Brajesh Pathak urges voters to focus on development Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak alleged that ration distribution was highly irregular before 2017, claiming that only a portion of allocated foodgrains reached beneficiaries. He said ration dealers were now receiving permanent shops and highlighted improvements in roads, electricity, water supply and education. He also said shops could now sell a wider range of goods, creating additional income opportunities. Pathak claimed that law and order had improved, contrasting the previous situation of alleged criminal influence with the current government. He urged voters not to vote on the basis of religion, caste or neighbourhood, but on the basis of development and the government's work. Minister claims major improvement in ration distribution Food and Civil Supplies Minister Manoj Kumar Pandey claimed that only 20% of ration was distributed before 2017, while 80% allegedly reached the black market. He said foodgrain distribution has increased from 23 lakh metric tonnes to 90 lakh metric tonnes. Pandey said the government had also improved access to ration for people with disabilities, visual impairments and others unable to travel to ration shops, allowing them to receive supplies at home. He highlighted improvements in farmers' access to MSP and said reports of starvation deaths from Bundelkhand had declined. He described the changes over the past nine years as a major transformation in Uttar Pradesh.

stories.title: Mother, daughter found with throats slit:Milkman discovers blood-soaked bodies at home; scooter rider visited two days ago
stories.summary: A mother and daughter were allegedly murdered by having their throats slit in Etawah, Uttar Pradesh,. The incident came to light at around 8am on Monday, when a milkman arrived at their home to make a delivery. He knocked on the gate repeatedly, but nobody opened it. The milkman then called the woman's husband, who works in Noida. He went to the back of the house and looked inside, where he saw Pushpa Devi Yadav (55) lying dead on the courtyard floor. Her daughter, Nirmala Devi alias Manju Devi (38), was found on a cot in a room around 10 metres away. A blood-stained sickle was lying on the cot. Police found blood trails from the room to the courtyard, indicating that Nirmala's body had been dragged there. Nirmala had reportedly been involved in a marital dispute with her in-laws for five years. Four months after her marriage, her husband and brothers-in-law allegedly assaulted her and sent her back to her maternal home. She had been living with her mother ever since, and a divorce case was also pending. On August 3, 2026, a court ordered her husband to pay ₹7,000 a month as maintenance. Neighbours said a young man on a scooter had been seen visiting the house on August 14 and 15. There had been no activity at the house since August 15. The family suspects that Nirmala's in-laws may have been behind the double murder. The incident took place in Chandethi village, under Bharthana police station, around 25 km from the district headquarters. Family lived in village while sons worked outside Chandethi resident Suresh Chandra (60) works as a security guard in Noida. His wife Pushpa and daughter Nirmala lived at their village home. Their elder son, Naval Kishore, drives an Ola cab in Noida, while their younger son, Nand Kishore, works for a private company in Pune. Milkman discovered the bodies Rajiv, a milk trader from the village, said he had been supplying milk to Suresh's family for several years. He arrived at the house at around 8am on Sunday, called out several times and knocked on the gate, but received no response. After around half an hour, he called Suresh and asked whether anyone was at home. Suresh said everyone was there. At his request, Rajiv went to the back of the house and looked inside, where he saw the bloodied bodies of Pushpa and Nirmala. On receiving information from Suresh, Bharthana police station in-charge Vikram Singh reached the spot with a police team. SSP Brijesh Srivastava also arrived to investigate. A forensic team and dog squad were called in, while both bodies were sent for post-mortem examination. Police seized the blood-stained sickle found on the cot. Milkman had found the gate locked a day earlier Rajiv said he had also visited the house on Sunday morning to deliver milk, but the gate was locked then as well. He returned at around 5pm on Sunday, but nobody opened the gate despite repeated knocking. This made him suspect that something was wrong. Scooter rider seen at house before murders During police questioning, neighbours said they had seen a young man on a scooter visiting Suresh's house on August 14 and 15. He was reportedly last seen outside the house at around 9 pm on August 15. Since then, neither the young man nor any activity from inside the house had been noticed. Daughter married in 2021, divorce case pending Nirmala married Satendra Kumar alias Manni in 2021 in the Kishni police station area of Mainpuri. She had no children. Four months after the wedding, her husband and brothers-in-law allegedly assaulted her and sent her back to her parents' home, where she had lived with her mother ever since. Her in-laws had also filed a divorce case, which remains pending in court. On August 3, 2026, the court ordered her husband to pay ₹7,000 per month in maintenance to Nirmala. ‘Attacker appears to have come with intent to kill’ SSP Brijesh Kumar Srivastava said no belongings inside the house appeared to have been disturbed. Prima facie, the murders did not appear to have been committed during a robbery. Police are primarily investigating Nirmala's long-running dispute with her in-laws. Investigators are also gathering information from people connected with the case and the family's acquaintances. The SSP said the case is expected to be solved soon with the help of the post-mortem and forensic reports.

stories.title: Son carries 95-year-old mother in Kanwar:3-km queue at Kashi Vishwanath, helicopter showers flowers in Bareilly
stories.summary: Today is the third Monday of Sawan, which also coincides with Nag Panchami. This rare combination has occurred after 23 years. Shiva temples across Uttar Pradesh have witnessed huge crowds of devotees and Kanwariyas since early morning. After the Mangala Aarti, the temple doors were opened for devotees at 4am. At Kashi Vishwanath Temple, a queue stretching for around 3 km has formed. Around 5 lakh devotees have already had darshan. Devotees carrying Ganga water began queuing from midnight for the Jalabhishek. Baba Vishwanath is giving darshan today in the Ardhanarishwar form. 95-year-old mother carried in Kanwar for 100 km In Firozabad, three sons carried their 95-year-old mother, Virma Devi, in a Kanwar and set out on a pilgrimage. They will travel around 100 km to Badaun. Her sons Om Prakash, Bhagirath Singh and Janak Singh, along with her grandchildren, are accompanying her. Mangala Aarti held at 2am in Kanpur At Anandeshwar Temple in Kanpur, the Mangala Aarti was performed at 2am, after which the temple doors were opened for devotees. At Baba Barkhandinath Temple in Bareilly, flowers were showered from a helicopter on devotees and Kanwariyas. As the flower shower began, devotees took out their mobile phones to record videos of the moment. See 3 pictures

stories.title: Black clouds hover in Gorakhpur, light rain begins:People step out with umbrellas and raincoats; temperature to reach 30°C
stories.summary: The weather has remained pleasant in Gorakhpur since Monday morning. Dark, dense clouds have covered the sky across several parts of the city, with light rain reported in some areas. The combination of rain and overcast conditions has brought a noticeable change in the weather, giving people some relief from the heat and humidity of the past few days. People head out with umbrellas and raincoats People travelling to school and work in the morning used umbrellas and raincoats to protect themselves from the rain. In several areas, commuters were seen travelling cautiously because of the wet roads and light showers. At the same time, some people were seen enjoying the pleasant weather, rain and cool winds. Similar weather conditions for two days Gorakhpur has experienced similar weather for the past two days, with cloudy skies followed by occasional light rain. The conditions have provided considerable relief from the scorching sunshine and heat. However, humidity has increased after the rain, making the weather feel muggy at times. Temperature drops by 3–4°C The change in weather has also affected temperatures. Compared with previous days, temperatures have fallen by around 3–4°C. As a result, people are experiencing less daytime heat than before. Rain likely due to low-pressure area According to meteorologist Dr Kailash Pandey, a low-pressure area has formed over Jharkhand. A cyclonic circulation is also present over western Uttar Pradesh at an altitude of around 5,000 feet. These weather systems could bring rain to Gorakhpur and surrounding areas. The maximum temperature in Gorakhpur is expected to be around 30°C today, while the minimum could be around 27°C. The drop in temperature is likely to keep conditions relatively pleasant. Humidity could reach 70–90% Despite the lower temperatures, humidity is expected to remain high. It could range between 70% and 90% today. As a result, people may continue to experience sticky and humid conditions even with rain and cloudy skies.

stories.title: Gen Alpha takes to streets in Lucknow, blocks highway:Students say no teachers in school; walk 8 km, principal secretary holds 2.5-hour talks
stories.summary: Around 250 Gen Alpha girl students took to the streets in Lucknow on Monday morning to protest against a shortage of teachers at their school. The students gathered at the Dubbaga-Kanpur Bypass crossing around 7 am amid heavy rain and blocked the road. The students had walked around 2.5km from the Jai Prakash Narayan Sarvodaya Girls’ School on Mohan Road to reach the crossing. The school, which serves students in Classes 6 to 12, is run by the Social Welfare Department. The protest caused traffic jams stretching 2- 3 km on all four sides of the bypass. Police were alerted, and teams from four police stations and outposts reached the spot. Officers tried to convince the students to end the protest for nearly two hours, but the girls insisted that the District Magistrate should come to the spot. When their demand was not accepted, the students started running towards the DM’s residence in Hazratganj. Police personnel followed them as they ran on the wrong side of the Lucknow-Hardoi Highway. When the students reached Balaganj crossing, around 8km from Mohan Road, ACP Kakori Shakeel Ahmed and ADCP Dhananjay stopped them and spoke to them. In their presence, the officers contacted Social Welfare Department officials over the phone and informed them about the students’ concerns. The officials assured the students that they would speak to them directly at the school. ACP Kakori told the students that their problems would be resolved on Monday itself. The students then agreed to end the protest and were sent back to the school in e-buses. Amid heavy rain, Social Welfare Department Principal Secretary Anurag Yadav, Secretary and Director Sanjeev Singh, Social Welfare Officer Anjani Kumar, and Sarojini Nagar SDM Abhishek Kumar Singh reached the school to meet the students. The officials held discussions with the students for around two and a half hours before leaving the school. See 2 pictures- ‘No teachers for Physics, Chemistry or Biology at school’ The students said their school does not have teachers for Physics, Chemistry or Biology. Despite repeatedly raising the issue over the past year, no action has been taken, leaving their studies severely affected. They also said they are unable to attend online classes because the school does not have a proper internet connection. Several students are also scheduled to appear for their board exams this year. स्कूल से बाहर निकलने पर प्रमुख सचिव अनुराग यादव ने बताया- बच्चों की बहुत बेसिक-सी मांगें हैं। सभी बच्चों से पर्सनल बात हुई है। फिजिक्स की टीचर मैटरनिटी लीव पर हैं। मैथ्स की टीचर अभी छुट्टी पर हैं। जल्द ही बच्चों को टीचर फुल लेंथ में मिल जाएंगे। स्कूल प्रशासन से संवाद की कमी के चलते आज ऐसा हुआ होगा। बच्चों ने दुर्भाग्य से ऐसा कर दिया। उन्होंने देखा होगा कि बगल के स्कूल के बच्चों ने ऐसा किया तो हम भी ऐसा करते हैं, जबकि ऐसी कोई बात नहीं थी। बच्चे बहुत अच्छे हैं। हमने जब उनकी सारी समस्याओं का समाधान बताया तो उन्होंने हमें भी विश्वास दिलाया कि अब ऐसा कभी नहीं करेंगे। समाज कल्याण विभाग के प्रमुख सचिव अनुराग यादव ने बताया कि करीब ढाई घंटे मैंने बच्चों से बात की। उन्होंने विश्वास दिलाया है कि अब ऐसा कभी नहीं करेंगे। 14 अगस्त को सर्वोदय विद्यालय के छात्र सड़क पर उतरे थे इससे पहले 14 अगस्त को इसी विद्यालय के बगल में स्थित सर्वोदय विद्यालय के छात्रों ने भी आगरा एक्सप्रेसवे से जुड़ने वाली लिंक रोड को जाम कर दिया था। उस जाम में विभाग के ही राज्यमंत्री असीम अरुण फंस गए थे। उन्होंने छात्रों को समझा-बुझाकर वापस स्कूल भेजा था और कहा था कि अपनी बात रखने का तरीका भले ही ठीक नहीं था, लेकिन उनकी बात मान लेना सराहना के योग्य है। Students had agreed after Minister Asim Arun’s assurance On 14 August, Minister of State for Social Welfare Asim Arun had said: “The Social Welfare Department runs two Sarvodaya schools in Lucknow. Guest teachers were arranged last year to address the shortage of teachers, but the High Court stayed the arrangement for some reason. The matter is scheduled to be heard on 17 August. We will strongly present the students’ concerns before the court. The children’s problem is our problem.”

stories.title: Ganga Expressway sinks 10 metres in Unnao:3-4 feet waterlogged in Prayagraj, NDRF rescues people by boat; rain alert across UP tomorrow
stories.summary: The monsoon has once again covered the entire state of Uttar Pradesh. On Monday, intermittent rain was reported in 65 cities, including Lucknow, Ghaziabad, Kanpur, Varanasi and Prayagraj. The situation worsened in Prayagraj after rain continued from late Sunday night. Three to four feet of water accumulated in colonies and lanes in the Kareli area, submerging cars and motorcycles. Many residents were forced to move to the first floors of their homes. Police and NDRF teams rescued several people and shifted them to safer locations. Lucknow received heavy rain for around four hours from 5 am. Roads and lanes in several areas were flooded. The city had recorded 40.9mm of rain on Sunday, the highest single-day rainfall of the season so far. In Unnao, a deep, around 10-metre-long crater developed on the Meerut-Prayagraj lane of the Ganga Expressway near Sonik at kilometre 421. The ground also caved in near the roadside railing. Meanwhile, more than 10 rivers, including the Ganga and Yamuna, are in spate across UP. Areas along the Ganga in Kanpur and Unnao have been flooded, with water entering more than 500 houses. Boats are being used on roads and in lanes, while many residents have been forced to stay on rooftops. Water levels in the Mandakini and Bardaha rivers are also rising in Chitrakoot, submerging the steps at Ramghat. In Varanasi, water has entered more than 100 small temples along the ghats. The Ratneshwar Mahadev and Brahmeshwar Mahadev temples are around 70% submerged. Sonbhadra recorded the highest rainfall in the state over the past 24 hours at 65.7mm. The Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts of UP on Tuesday. Schools in Hardoi and Jaunpur will remain closed on Tuesday due to the rain. See photos of rain- Monsoon to remain active for three more days According to Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh: “The low-pressure area that formed over the north-west Bay of Bengal is moving across Jharkhand and northern Chhattisgarh. It is gradually weakening as it moves further. However, its influence will strengthen the monsoon over northern India once again. Its impact is also being felt in Uttar Pradesh, where good rainfall is being recorded. The weather is expected to remain similar over the next three days.”

stories.title: Mother donates kidney to save son's life:₹7 lakh transplant fails in Mohali; both fall ill, family sells 1 bigha land for treatment
stories.summary: Altaf’s mother donated her kidney to save life of the son she had given birth to. However, after the transplant at a private hospital in Mohali, the transplanted kidney reportedly failed. As Altaf’s health deteriorated, his father took him to PGI Chandigarh. He remained admitted there for around eight days, but his condition did not improve. He now requires dialysis every third day. The family goes to PGI for dialysis at ₹500, but if they do not get a slot, they have to pay ₹3,000 at a private centre. With treatment costs mounting, the family even had to sell their one bigha of land. Altaf and his father shared their ordeal while speaking outside PGI. Know the complete case in sequence Worked as a driver in Abu Dhabi for five years Altaf is a resident of Najibabad tehsil in Bijnor, Uttar Pradesh. He worked as a driver in Abu Dhabi for around five years. Initially, he earned ₹20,000 a month, while his monthly income had risen to around ₹25,000 by the time he returned to India. Altaf is married but has no children. Sudden leg pain led to discovery of kidney disease One day, Altaf suddenly developed severe pain in his leg, followed by swelling. He received treatment in Abu Dhabi and was later discharged. His family then brought him back to India. After medical examinations in Bijnor, doctors found that he had kidney problems. Mother decided to donate her kidney When a kidney transplant became necessary, Altaf’s mother, Sherunika, decided to donate one of her kidneys. According to the family, Sherunika had previously suffered from kidney stones. His father, Shahid, had informed the doctors about this before the transplant. Transplant performed in Mohali in October 2025 Altaf underwent a kidney transplant at a private hospital in Mohali in October 2025. According to the family, the procedure cost around ₹7 lakh. The family hoped the transplant would improve Altaf’s health and allow him to return to a normal life. However, his condition began deteriorating again after some time. The family says the transplanted kidney subsequently failed. Taken to PGI for further treatment After Altaf’s condition worsened, his family took him to PGI Chandigarh in July 2026. He remained admitted there for around eight days before being discharged. However, he continued to require dialysis. The family now takes him to an outside dialysis centre every third day, where each session costs around ₹3,000. Altaf is unable to speak, so his family understands his daily needs and problems through his gestures and physical condition. Mother’s health also deteriorated after donating kidney Altaf’s mother, Sherunika, has also frequently been unwell since donating her kidney. According to the family, she suffers from stomach pain and intermittent fever. While Altaf’s treatment continues, Sherunika’s health has also become a concern. His father, Shahid, is looking after both of them. Family now has to arrange ₹3,000 every third day Altaf, who once worked as a driver in Abu Dhabi, is now dependent on regular medical treatment. According to the family, around ₹9.5 lakh has been spent on the transplant and subsequent treatment. The family has also sold one bigha of land to meet the medical expenses. Altaf now requires dialysis every third day, costing around ₹3,000 per session. As he cannot speak, his father Shahid is responsible for arranging his treatment and covering the expenses. The family’s biggest challenge now is ensuring that Altaf’s treatment continues without interruption.

stories.title: Stomach surgery leads to hand being severed twice:Lucknow mother blames doctors’ negligence for ruining son’s life
stories.summary: Ankit Rathore, 21, from Firozabad, underwent stomach surgery at Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital in Lucknow. He later had to undergo two amputations of his left arm. Ankit alleges that a cannula was inserted into his hand for an intravenous drip. Around 24 hours later, his left hand began to swell. His mother, Pushpa Devi, alleges medical negligence and says, “He was my only son and my support in old age, but now he has become dependent on others.” The family complained to the Chief Minister and Deputy Chief Minister about the alleged negligence. At Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak’s residence, a doctor from Lohia Hospital said there had been no deficiency in treatment and suggested that Ankit may have moved his hand while the drip was being administered, causing an infection. His mother broke down on hearing this and said, “My son was unconscious. How could he have moved his hand? You have ruined my son’s life.” The family is currently sitting outside the Chief Minister’s residence, hoping for action against those responsible. Now, the complete story in sequence... The problem began when food started getting stuck in Ankit’s food pipe Ankit’s family lives in the Nai Basti area of Firozabad. His father, Mahesh Chandra, works as a labourer, while his mother Pushpa Devi and two sisters live with him. Ankit used to sell fruit and vegetables from a roadside stall. About a year ago, he developed stomach pain. Doctors told him that food was getting stuck in his food pipe and referred him to Saifai Medical College. As he did not improve, he eventually went to Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital in Lucknow. Ankit says he was admitted on June 2, 2026, where gastroenterologist Dr Hitesh Sharda treated him. His operation was scheduled for June 8. He entered the operating theatre at 9am and came out at 8pm. His hand was already hurting, but staff told him this was normal after surgery. The pain continued throughout the night. The next day, his hand had swollen considerably and the pain had become severe. Another Lohia Hospital doctor examined him and said treatment would have been possible only within the first six hours. Dr Hitesh Sharda subsequently operated on the hand, but it did not improve. Ankit says several nerves appeared to have been damaged and his hand began turning black. When he raised the issue with the doctor, he was allegedly told, “I am a stomach doctor, not a hand doctor.” PGI and KGMU refused to admit him On June 20, Lohia doctors referred Ankit elsewhere. At PGI, doctors reportedly said his case was complicated and did not admit him. KGMU also refused admission. For three days, Ankit moved between hospitals, sleeping at a railway station at night and sitting outside government hospitals during the day. On June 24, he was readmitted to Lohia Hospital and his arm was amputated below the elbow. When the infection continued to spread, doctors amputated it again on July 22, this time above the elbow. Mother says: ‘We came for a stomach operation, but lost a hand’ Ankit’s mother Pushpa and sister Lakshmi remained with him during his treatment. Pushpa says Ankit’s father was so distressed by his condition that his memory began to weaken. When Ankit’s condition deteriorated, the family somehow took him to Firozabad. Pushpa says they could not return home because they had gone to Lucknow for a stomach operation but their son had instead lost his arm. ‘When we complained, our belongings were thrown out’ Lakshmi says the family approached the CMO’s office, Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak and the Chief Minister’s residence seeking action. She alleges that after they complained, Lohia Hospital staff threw their belongings outside and stopped the free food and drink they had been receiving. She also claims the family was accused of seeking government jobs for Ankit and Lakshmi. According to her, officials said they had provided ₹1 lakh and offered to arrange prosthetic arms. Lakshmi denies these claims and says they did not even speak to the family properly. She says she also filed an RTI seeking details of what the doctors who examined Ankit had recorded, but the information was not provided. ‘We were not allowed to meet the Chief Minister again’ Pushpa says the family met the Chief Minister on July 13. According to her, he heard their complaint and ordered officials to take action against those responsible. She showed the complaint carrying the Chief Minister’s Jan Darbar stamp, which was forwarded by the CM’s office to the DM/CMO. Pushpa says the family tried to meet the Chief Minister twice more but was not allowed to do so. On the fourth attempt, they took Ankit with them, but were stopped outside. Ankit was taken inside, but was not allowed to meet the CM. Pushpa also says she visited Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak’s residence four times. She alleges that Lohia doctors’ discharge papers repeatedly blamed the family rather than acknowledging any lapse. ‘I can comment only after looking into the matter’ Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Lucknow DM Vishakh G. He said- I am not aware of what happened in this matter. I can comment only after properly looking into it.
