stories.title: UP to recruit 1 lakh outsourced workers:Existing staff to get salary hike of up to ₹15,000; know what benefits they will receive
stories.summary: One lakh new employees will be recruited on an outsourced basis in Uttar Pradesh government departments. At the same time, preparations are underway to increase the salaries of more than 2.75 lakh existing outsourced employees by ₹8,000 to ₹15,000. Five months ago, in the election year, the Yogi government had increased the salaries of 2.75 lakh outsourced employees by ₹8,000 to ₹10,000. The Uttar Pradesh Outsourced Services Corporation (UPCAS) is now expected to become operational before August 30, with Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath scheduled to inaugurate it. Government departments will provide vacancy details to the corporation According to a government official, departments will no longer directly select agencies for outsourced recruitment. They will inform the corporation about the number of employees currently working, additional manpower required and the applicable salary structure. The corporation will then select agencies through the GeM portal. What was the problem earlier? Previously, different agencies appointed employees on contracts. There were allegations of exploitation, including delayed payment and employees not receiving the fixed honorarium. Outsourced employees to receive these benefits Honorarium by the 5th of every month: Employees will receive their monthly honorarium directly in their bank accounts by the 5th. Vendors failing to pay on time will face penalties. A company receiving more than three consecutive complaints that are found to be genuine may be blacklisted. 26 working days and weekly holiday: Employees will work for 26 days a month and receive a weekly holiday. Regular training will also be provided to improve efficiency. Female employees will be entitled to maternity leave. PF, ESI and insurance: Along with the honorarium, 13% EPF and 3.25% ESI contributions must be deposited on time. The corporation will monitor these payments. Employees will also receive mediclaim and accidental insurance cover. ₹15,000 funeral assistance: If an employee dies while in service, their family will receive ₹15,000 towards funeral expenses. Selection through written test and interview New employees will be selected through a written examination and interview. Reservations will include 21% for Scheduled Castes (SC), 2% for Scheduled Tribes (ST), 27% for Other Backward Classes (OBC) and 10% for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS). The system is expected to make recruitment more transparent. Existing outsourced employees will not be removed and will continue working according to the tender conditions. These 10 departments have the most outsourced employees Urban Local Bodies Medical and Health Medical Education Energy Transport Women and Child Welfare Agriculture Industrial Development MSME Labour Department Employees hope old vendor-related complaints will end Outsourced employees expect the new corporation to address long-standing complaints against vendors, including: Taking money before joining: Some vendors allegedly demand one to two months' remuneration in advance before offering jobs. Deduction from remuneration: There are frequent complaints that vendors take back 10–20% of employees' remuneration in cash. Arbitrary recruitment: Vendors and officials are allegedly accused of colluding to appoint preferred candidates, denying deserving applicants opportunities. Removal without notice: Employees have alleged that vendors and officials sometimes terminate their services without prior notice. Transfer as punishment: Instead of removing an employee after a mistake, officials sometimes transfer them to another office, which employees say does not resolve the underlying issue. Corporation formed last year, but work has not started CM Yogi Adityanath announced the formation of a corporation for outsourced recruitment in the 2025–26 Budget. The government subsequently established the Uttar Pradesh Outsourced Services Corporation in September last year and appointed IAS officer Amrita Soni as its Managing Director. The Secretariat Administration Department is the nodal department. An office is also being prepared at the Pickup Building. Although nearly a year has passed since the corporation was formed, it has not yet begun operations. The government is now preparing to make it functional this month. Budget increased by ₹426 crore; ₹20 crore approved for corporation CM Yogi had announced the salary increase in the Assembly, following which the government increased the budget by ₹426 crore and released ₹2,223.84 crore. The UP Cabinet has also approved ₹20 crore at zero interest to support the operation of the Uttar Pradesh Outsourced Services Corporation.

stories.title: Man takes selfie with 11-month-old daughter, throws her into Yamuna:Couple fought on moving bike; girl’s birthday was 3 days away
stories.summary: A father threw his 11-month-old daughter into the Yamuna after a fight with his wife in Agra. Before this, he also took a selfie with his daughter. After throwing his daughter, the father started pushing his wife into the river. When the woman screamed, a crowd of people passing by on the bridge gathered. Passersby somehow rescued his wife by freeing her from the husband. The wife said - We were going to Agra to buy clothes for our daughter. Her birthday was three days later, on 17 August. On the way, my husband stopped the bike on the bridge on the pretext of taking photos. After that, he threw our daughter into the river. After hearing the woman's account, the passersby severely beat up the accused husband. After that, they handed him over to the police. The incident occurred on Friday at 3 PM at Akbara Bridge in Sikandra. A video of this has also surfaced on social media. 2 images related to the incident Now read the complete case Rinku, a resident of Badmaghi village in Baldev, was going to the market on a bike with his wife Lakshmi and their 11-month-old daughter. On the way, he got into an argument with his wife over something. Rinku suddenly stopped the bike on Akbara bridge. He told his wife that he wanted to take a photo with their daughter. Rinku took a selfie with his daughter. Immediately after this, he threw his daughter into the Yamuna River. As soon as his wife ran to the bridge railing, Rinku started pushing her into the river as well. But when Lakshmi raised an alarm, passersby on the bridge gathered at the spot. Husband became aggressive when people beat him Lakshmi told the passersby that her husband had thrown their daughter into the Yamuna. Now, he is trying to push me into the river too. As soon as people heard this, they became enraged. After rescuing the wife from her husband, they started beating him. During this, Rinku also became aggressive towards the people. Upon receiving information, the police team reached the spot. The accused Rinku was taken into custody and sent to the police station. Meanwhile, a search operation has been started in the Yamuna River to find the child. Wife said - We were going to Agra to buy clothes for daughter Laxmi said, ‘’My marriage took place on 14 June, 2024. After marriage, I started being harassed for dowry. My in-laws threw me out of the house. I stayed at my maternal home in the village of Jatoli Kadmi Deeg, Bharatpur for 6 months. After that, my husband called me back. He was not happy about having a daughter. He used to quarrel every day. For the past two to three days, Rinku's behavior had changed. He was pretending to love the child. Today he said, let's go to Agra. We need to buy clothes for the child. As soon as we reached Yamuna Bridge, Rinku stopped the bike. He said he wanted to take photos with the child.'' 'Husband killed only daughter before her birthday' Mother Laxmi said that I had only one daughter. Her birthday was on 17 August. My husband Rinku took my daughter's life before that. I had no idea that he was planning to kill the child. DCP City Syed Ali Abbas said - In the Sikandra area, a man threw his daughter into the Yamuna from a bridge. PAC divers have been deployed into the river. The divers are conducting a search operation in the river for the girl. The accused husband is being interrogated regarding the incident. Domestic discord has emerged during the investigation.

stories.title: Naib tehsildar’s car runs over grandfather-grandson, kills both:Angry crowd surrounds vehicle in Hathras; police rescue staff
stories.summary: A road accident occurred on Friday around 7 PM on the Mathura-Bareilly National Highway in Hathras. The vehicle of the Naib Tehsildar of Sikandra Rau collided with two oncoming motorcycles. A grandfather and his 6-year-old grandson riding on one motorcycle died on the spot in the accident. Meanwhile, the youth riding on the second motorcycle was seriously injured. The police have taken him to the hospital. The bodies have been sent for post-mortem. Angry people blocked the road, after the accident. The police cleared the traffic after persuading them. The incident is from near Salempur village in the Hathras Junction police station area. Now know the complete matter 56-year-old Subhash Chandra, a resident of village Thulai, was a farmer. He had a 6-year-old grandson named Daksh. On Friday evening, both were returning to the village on a bike. Subhash was riding the bike, and Daksh was sitting with him. During this time, the vehicle of the Naib Tehsildar, coming from the opposite direction, collided with their bike. Subhash and Daksh died on the spot after the collision. Meanwhile, Sonu from the same village, who was riding another bike, was seriously injured. The police took him to the district hospital, from where doctors referred him to Aligarh in critical condition. Both bodies were sent for post-mortem. Villagers surrounded the vehicle and created a commotion After the accident, a large number of villagers gathered at the spot. They surrounded the Naib Tehsildar's vehicle and started a commotion. During this time, the vehicle was also vandalized. The villagers raised slogans against the police and administration. They also had an altercation with the officials present at the spot. Police rescued officers and employees from the crowd As soon as the information was received, police reached the spot. Police safely evacuated the Naib Tehsildar and other employees from the crowd. Considering the situation, police force from several stations was called to the spot. Upon receiving information about the incident, Additional District Magistrate Sadar and Additional District Magistrate Sasni, along with other officers, also reached. Villagers blocked the highway for some time. Officers pacified them by counseling, after which the jam was cleared. Police have sent both bodies for post-mortem and have started an investigation into the accident.

stories.title: ATS picks up 2 suspects from Hapur mosque:Siblings in Kanpur under suspicion of Pakistan links; major action ahead of 15 August
stories.summary: UP ATS and the Central Intelligence Agency detained four suspicious individuals in Kanpur Dehat and Hapur a day before Independence Day. Two people were apprehended from each location. The first operation took place in the Bahadurgarh area of Hapur on Friday around 5 AM. The UP ATS team detained two suspicious youths from a mosque. Both had arrived at the mosque on a bike. Shortly after, the ATS team reached the mosque. Both were taken to Meerut for interrogation. The second operation took place in Bara village of Kanpur Dehat on Wednesday. Here, the Central Agency team detained a brother and sister. The team searched the house for about 30 minutes and confiscated mobile phones of all family members. Kanpur Dehat police received information about this on Friday. In both cases, there is suspicion that the suspects have contact with Pakistan and are involved in monetary transactions. However, no official confirmation of any suspect's Pakistani connection has been made yet. First, know about the action in Hapur Dehat According to the Masjid Intazamiya Committee, both youths arrived at the Qureshiyan Mosque located in Sherpur village under Bahadurgarh police station area on a bike around 5 am on Friday. They parked their bike outside the mosque and went inside. Just 10 minutes later, the ATS Meerut team arrived. Both were taken into custody. Both youths had reached the mosque without any prior acquaintance. According to local people, they have been identified as Mohammad Sameer and Salman. Information has been received that both work in a local factory. However, their identity and the reason for reaching the mosque have not been officially confirmed. According to local people, the ATS team reached there just a few minutes after both reached the mosque. This suggests that the agency was already monitoring their activities. However, no official information has been given by the police or ATS in this regard. Police said- The situation will be clear after investigation Security agencies are gathering information about the identity of both youths, their local contacts, purpose of reaching the mosque, and recent activities. Their mobile phones and items found with them are also being examined. Bahadurgarh police station in-charge Indrakant Yadav informed that information has been received through social media about two suspicious youths being caught at Qureshiyan Mosque in Sherpur village. Both are said to be residents of another area. ATS has taken them into custody. The matter is being investigated. Now know about the action in Kanpur Dehat On Wednesday morning, a team from security and intelligence agencies arrived in three vehicles at Bara village in Akbarpur Kotwali area. The team searched the house of Bakar Khan (30) and his sister Uruj Fatima (32) for about 30 minutes. After this, both were taken into custody and taken to Delhi for questioning. Mobile phones of other family members have also been seized for examination. Local police received information about the case on Friday. According to sources, agencies suspect that Bakar Khan and Uruj Fatima have contacts with Pakistan. Allegations of money transactions with Pakistan against both are also being investigated. It has emerged that investigating agencies found suspicious chats in their mobile phones and digital activities. Agencies are trying to find out who they were in contact with and what their relationship is with people present in Pakistan. Pakistani citizens also own land in Bara village Bakar Khan's mother said that on Wednesday around 6:30 AM, about 10 people arrived at their house in three vehicles. They showed their identity cards and said they had come from Delhi. After that, the officials started searching the house. They checked every single item kept in the house. They also checked the mobile phones of family members. After searching for about 30 minutes, the officials took Bakar Khan and Uruj Fatima along with their mobile phones with them. The team also confiscated the mobile phone of their younger daughter. The mother says that it has been about 60 hours since both were taken away, but the family has not received any information about them. Many people from Bara village have relatives living in Pakistan. Some Pakistani citizens also own land in the village, which has now been declared enemy property. It is being reported that local families cultivate this land. SP said - We don't have information about the case yet Kanpur Dehat SP Shraddha Narendra Pandey said that- A team from the Central Agency had come. While investigating a case, the team took both Bakar Khan and Uruj Fatima along with them. What the case is about, we don't have information about it. Kanpur Dehat Police received information about the case through ATS Kanpur Unit. After which the local police is also investigating the matter

stories.title: ‘How dare it bite me’:Man bites cobra after killing it; snake had bitten him three times
stories.summary: A young man confronted a cobra under the influence of alcohol in Barabanki. The snake bit the young man three times. Even after this, the young man did not let go of the snake. He wrapped it around his wrist. The snake kept biting the young man, but he did not release it. He killed the snake and then tried to bite it with his mouth. Neighbors kept trying to get the snake away from the young man, but he did not agree. On one side, 4-5 people were pulling the snake; on the other side was the young man. He was muttering angrily...how dare it bite me. The incident occurred on Thursday at 8 pm; the video surfaced on Friday. First see 2 pictures... Cobra emerged from neighbor's house In the village of Bairanaamau Manjhari in Mohammadpur Khala, Sanjay (35), son of Sonelal, lives with his family. The family includes two children, his parents, and a sister. His wife has passed away. The young man is a farmer. On Thursday around 8 PM, a cobra snake emerged at neighbor Chandar Yadav's house. Sonelal arrived intoxicated and started trying to catch the snake. Roamed around village with dead snake in hand Even after being bitten three times by the snake, Sanjay did not relent. He caught the snake and killed it with a stick. He started roaming around the house with the dead snake in his hand. Seeing him roam like this, crowd gathered. Neighbors stopped Sanjay and advised him to get treatment. A video of the incident has also surfaced, in which Sanjay's sister Rekha and some villagers are trying to make him release the snake, but he is not ready to let it go. Attempted to bite the dead snake In an intoxicated state, Sanjay was repeatedly saying, 'This will bite me; how dare it.' People kept trying to explain, but he was not ready to listen to anyone. Sanjay even tried to bite the dead snake with his teeth. According to the villagers, the snake was about three and a half feet long. Village head representative Sher Bahadur, Ramchander, RK Chauhan, Ramlakhan, Baithu, and Subedar, along with others, identified the snake as a cobra. The youth's family members and villagers somehow calmed him down. Even after being bitten by the snake three times, Sanjay was not ready to go to the hospital. Reached CHC after an hour; doctors sent him home The village head was informed about the incident about an hour after the snake bite. After this, the village head immediately took the youth along with his family members to CHC Suratganj. Doctors gave him an anti-venom injection and administered glucose. He was sent home after his condition became normal. According to villagers, the police were not informed about the incident. CHC Superintendent Dr. Rajarshi Tripathi said that such actions should not be taken after a snake bite. After a snake bite, one should immediately go to the hospital without wasting time. The youth was sent home after his condition became normal.

stories.title: Teacher dies inside car:Wife breaks down, daughter cries, ‘Papa, wake up, let’s go home’
stories.summary: A government teacher died while sitting in his car in Sitapur. His body was found around 10 AM on Friday morning, in the seat next to the driver in a car parked by the roadside. The car door was open. Seeing the car parked for a long time, nearby shopkeepers became suspicious. They went closer, called out, and shook the body, but there was no movement. Upon receiving information, the police arrived at the scene. Shortly after, the wife and daughter of teacher Radheshyam Patel (50) arrived at the scene. Seeing her husband's body, the wife became distraught. She clung to the body and started crying. The daughter, crying, said - 'Dad, you just left home, please get up and let's go home.' Death is suspected to be due to a heart attack. Police have sent the body for post-mortem. The incident occurred near the Fire Brigade Office in the city Kotwali area. See two pictures related to the incident Going to school by car, it got a puncture on the way Radheshyam Patel, a resident of Ismailpur locality in Kotwali Dehat, was a teacher at the aided school Janata Madhyamik Vidyalaya Sonari. Besides his wife Anuradha Patel, the family includes a daughter Yashasvi (21) and a son Anoop (18). The family said that Radheshyam left for school at 7:30 AM on Friday in his Maruti-800 car. He had travelled 15 km from home when suddenly the car's rear tire punctured. He stopped the car on the roadside and started changing the tire himself. Eyewitness shopkeeper said - took out the spare tire then sat in the car Eyewitness shopkeeper Azhar said - When the tire punctured, he himself took out the spare tire to change it. He took the tire out of the boot and placed it near the car. Then perhaps he suddenly felt some anxiety. He went and sat in the car. After that, he did not come out of the car again. According to Azhar, we thought he might have sat in the car due to fatigue. So we didn't pay much attention. I got busy with bike servicing work in the shop. About two hours later, by 10 o'clock, the car was still seen standing there. Its door was open. When we became suspicious, we went closer. There we saw that he was lying unconscious on the car seat. We tried to wake him up. But when there was no movement, we informed the police. Police arrived at the scene. They gathered information from the people nearby. Clerk who worked with him informed the daughter Retired clerk Sushil Kumar Srivastava, who had worked with the teacher, said - My house is in the lane opposite to where Radheshyam's car broke down. I retired from this school 6 months ago. I received a call from the school cook saying that Radheshyam had not come to school today. I called his daughter and found out that he had left in the morning. Meanwhile, a boy from the neighbourhood informed that Radheshyam sir's car was parked in front, and he was found unconscious in the car. After this, I reached the spot. stories.summary: Allahabad High Court Lucknow Bench: राष्ट्र की सुरक्षा में लगभग 38 वर्षों तक अपनी सेवाएं देने वाले पूर्व वायुवीर इन्द्रेश कुमार को आखिरकार न्याय मिल गया। इलाहाबाद उच्च न्यायालय की लखनऊ पीठ ने एक महत्वपूर्ण और दूरगामी प्रभाव वाले निर्णय में भारत सरकार, रक्षा मंत्रालय द्वारा दायर याचिका को खारिज करते हुए पूर्व वायुसेना कर्मी के दिव्यांगता पेंशन के अधिकार को बरकरार रखा है। न्यायालय ने स्पष्ट निर्देश दिया है कि पूर्व वायुवीर को तत्काल प्रभाव से नियमानुसार दिव्यांगता पेंशन तथा उससे संबंधित सभी लाभ उपलब्ध कराए जाएं। यह फैसला न केवल इन्द्रेश कुमार के लिए राहत लेकर आया है, बल्कि देशभर के पूर्व सैनिकों और सशस्त्र बलों के कर्मियों के अधिकारों की दृष्टि से भी एक महत्वपूर्ण नजीर माना जा रहा है।

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi’s Savarkar defamation case quashed by SC:Required sanction was not obtained; case relates to 2022 Bharat Jodo Yatra remarks
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday quashes a defamation case against Congress MP Rahul Gandhi over alleged objectionable remarks against Veer Savarkar and spreading hatred in society. The Uttar Pradesh government tells the court that official sanction to prosecute Rahul Gandhi was not obtained. The Supreme Court says that without the required legal sanction, the case cannot continue. A bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Sheel Nagu heard the matter. The court said in its decision- In the affidavit filed by the government, the Additional Solicitor General and the complainant's lawyer have admitted that the necessary sanction was not obtained in this case. In such a situation, the complaint and all orders issued by the magistrate are quashed. Made remarks against Savarkar in November 2022 The controversy is related to a speech given by Rahul Gandhi during his 'Bharat Jodo Yatra'. Addressing a rally in Akola district of Maharashtra on November 17, 2022, Rahul had made remarks against Savarkar. Following this, advocate Nripendra Pandey had filed a private criminal complaint against him. It was alleged that Rahul deliberately insulted Savarkar. His comment was a well-thought-out conspiracy to defame Savarkar. High Court's order was challenged in the Supreme Court The lower court (Magistrate Court) had taken cognisance of this complaint and issued a summons to Rahul Gandhi. Against this, Rahul Gandhi had approached the High Court. The Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court, while hearing the petition on April 4, 2025, had said that Rahul Gandhi can file a review petition in the Sessions Court, and therefore, there is no need for the High Court's intervention at this stage. Rahul Gandhi had challenged this decision of the High Court and the summons order in the Supreme Court.

stories.title: Yogi calls Congress-SP responsible for 1947 killings:Says, 'No one could have harmed India if Modi had been PM then'
stories.summary: CM Yogi responds to Shivpal Yadav’s remark about Azam Khan, accusing the SP of wanting to make him home minister and of triggering riots if it returns to power. Speaking at a Partition Horrors Remembrance Day event in Lucknow on Friday, Yogi Adityanath said SP leaders were now defending a person after whom a university was built, alleging that he was responsible for India’s Partition and Independence-related events. Without naming Azam Khan, Yogi said, “They are saying that if we come to power, we will make him home minister. They want to trigger riots again.” He also alleged that the person had arranged for rioters from Muzaffarnagar and Saharanpur to be brought to the then chief minister’s residence and honoured. Yogi said, “Look at the shameful thinking of these people. They are making such arguments in support of someone who got the rioters of Muzaffarnagar and Saharanpur honoured at the then CM’s residence.” Yogi’s remarks came two days after Shivpal Yadav met Azam Khan, who is lodged in Rampur jail, and said that the SP would make him home minister if it formed the government and would avenge all the alleged injustices against him. Earlier on Friday, the BJP organised a silent march in Lucknow. Yogi, wearing a mask, participated in the half-kilometre march before addressing the programme at Lok Bhawan. Key points from CM Yogi’s speech Yogi also targeted Congress, accusing it of betraying the country. He said Congress leaders remained silent in 1947 and wanted to gain power by any means. He alleged that the party’s intentions remain unchanged even today. He said Sanatanis, Sindhis and Punjabis were driven away from the places where they were born during Partition, while land that Pakistan had not even asked for was handed over to it. 1. ‘The Sanatan nation was divided for the sake of power’ CM Yogi said the entire country was observing Partition Horrors Remembrance Day, calling it one of the darkest chapters in the history of humanity. He said crores of Hindus were forced to leave their own motherland and birthplace, while lakhs of Hindus, Buddhists, Sikhs and Jains were massacred, with no one listening to their suffering. Yogi said the lust for power had reached such a level that a Sanatan nation was divided. He added that the day should also encourage people to learn from those dark chapters of history, as merely remembering the tragedy would not solve the problem. He questioned why the crisis occurred, who was responsible for it, how many perpetrators were punished, and how long India would continue to pay the price for Partition. 2. ‘Hindus were massacred in Bangladesh, but these parties remained silent’ Yogi said the questions surrounding Partition still remain before the country today. He said history should not be treated merely as a subject to study for exams, but as an opportunity to take pride in India’s glorious past and learn from and correct past mistakes. He said this was the thinking behind Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s decision to observe Partition Horrors Remembrance Day. Yogi alleged that those who remained silent in 1947 and were focused only on gaining power continue to follow the same approach even today. He said they have aimed to gain power at the cost of the country. “You must have seen the massacre of Hindus in Bangladesh, but these parties remained silent even then,” Yogi said. He alleged that they feared speaking out would upset their vote bank. He further accused such parties of treating power as personal property and a family inheritance for their own interests. According to Yogi, this mindset leads them to betray the country and create chaos and disorder. 3. ‘India was enslaved because of internal divisions and caste, regional differences’ CM Yogi said there were two major reasons why India became enslaved: internal differences and divisions based on caste and region. He said conspiracies continued alongside these divisions, and those behind them succeeded. As a result, the country was enslaved because people could not fight together. “People thought, ‘The attack is happening to someone else; why should I speak?’ The entire country had to pay the price for this,” Yogi said, adding that even India, which had remained united since ancient times, was eventually divided. 4. ‘Attempts were made to trigger riots in UP over the CAA’ Yogi said he was surprised when Prime Minister Narendra Modi introduced the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA). He said there was no reason to oppose the legislation, which provided citizenship to Hindus, Jains, Buddhists, Parsis and Christians who had been persecuted and forced to leave Afghanistan, Pakistan or Bangladesh and had lived in India for at least five years. “There was nothing in it about taking away the land of Muslims, Congress or the Samajwadi Party,” he said. However, he alleged that attempts were made to organise protests and trigger riots at several places in Uttar Pradesh, including Lucknow, Kanpur, Meerut, Bulandshahr, Muzaffarnagar and Saharanpur. Yogi said it was fortunate that Uttar Pradesh had a “double-engine” government at the time. He questioned why the CAA was being opposed and alleged that the SP and Congress were supporting the protests from behind. He also called these parties the “real culprits” of the 1947 Partition and said, “If Narendra Modi had been the prime minister at that time, no one could have harmed India.” Azam had built university in Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar’s name The CM also referred to the university established by SP leader Azam Khan in the name of Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar. Azam Khan established Jauhar University in 2005. It was named after renowned freedom fighter Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar, who led several movements against British rule. Mohammad Ali Jauhar served as president of both the Muslim League and the Congress. After India’s Independence, most members of his family moved to Pakistan. On 15 July, the Rampur district magistrate ordered the demolition of 38 of the university’s 40 buildings. However, Moradabad Divisional Commissioner Anjaneya Singh’s court stayed the DM’s order. The matter is currently pending before the court. See 2 pictures-

stories.title: 16-year-old kills father, then dies after jumping before metro:Angry over restrictions; mother lived separately in Noida
stories.summary: A 16-year-old boy allegedly killed his father while he was asleep in Noida and later died by suicide after jumping in front of a Metro train, police said. After the alleged killing, the teenager changed his blood-stained clothes, placed a photograph of his father in the room and offered a garland as a tribute. He then locked the room, took his father's mobile phone and bag, and went to a Metro station. After spending some time at the station, he jumped in front of a train. Police found his father's mobile phone and the room key in the teenager's bag. They contacted his mother, who arrived at the spot along with the boy's uncle. During questioning, the family told police that the teenager lived with his father, while his mother lived separately in Noida. Father found dead inside locked room The police took the boy's mother and uncle to the room on Thursday night. They opened the door with the key and found the body of 45-year-old Raju Sharma inside. Initial investigation suggested that Raju had imposed several restrictions on his son's movements. He had also stopped the boy's studies after Class 11. Police suspect that the teenager was distressed by these restrictions and allegedly killed his father early on Wednesday, August 12. He died by suicide at around 7am the same day. The incident took place in the Phase 3 police station area of Noida. Raju was a private tutor. He had divorced his wife 12 years ago and had been living with his only son. Raju lived in Noida for 21 years Raju was originally from Bokaro Steel City in Jharkhand. His father had worked for SAIL. Raju moved to Noida with his wife in 2005. He later lived with his only son in a rented room in the Ajnara Society area. He held an MCom degree and taught children through private tuition and online classes. Blood stains found inside room Police said the teenager's body was found near a railway line on Wednesday. During a search, officers found his father's mobile phone and the room key in his bag. Police used the mobile phone to contact his mother, who arrived and identified her son's body. Raju's brother, Arun Sharma, also reached the spot and told police that his brother was missing. The police questioned the mother, who said Raju had a short temper and had imposed several restrictions on his son. She said the teenager was often upset by them. This led police to suspect that the teenager might have killed his father before taking his own life. Police then took the mother and uncle to Raju's room. A strong smell was coming from inside. When they opened the door, they found Raju's body. Blood-stained clothes believed to belong to the teenager were found inside the room, along with blood stains on the walls. A forensic team collected samples from the scene, while the blood-stained clothes were sent to a laboratory for examination. Neighbours noticed little interaction between father and son Neighbour Kaushal said he rarely saw the teenager outside the house. The boy mostly stayed indoors and was only occasionally seen when he went upstairs to dry clothes. Ram Avtar Tiwari, another resident of the building, said the father and son rarely spoke to each other. He said the teenager prepared his own food and collected water himself. The father and son would generally exchange things only when necessary.

stories.title: Computer operator beaten to death:Names attackers in video before dying; FIR against 6, including former block chief and ration dealer
stories.summary: A computer operator with the Supply Department in Pratapgarh was beaten to death. At around 7 pm on Thursday, he was returning home from work when the accused, who were lying in wait, attacked him with sticks, iron rods and the butt of a revolver. The attackers fled after leaving him, believing he was dead. Family members reached the spot after being informed by local residents and took him to hospital. Doctors declared him dead. Before his death, the computer operator named six attackers, including a former block chief. A video of his statement has also surfaced. The incident took place in the Lilapur police station area, around 15 km from the district headquarters. Based on a complaint by the family, police have registered an FIR against six named accused, including the former block chief and his brother, who is a ration dealer. The 32-year-old computer operator, Saurabh Vishwakarma, got married a year ago. He has a four-month-old daughter. His wife, Aanchal, broke down after seeing her husband's body. Here is the full case in sequence Saurabh Vishwakarma (32), a resident of Sindhora village in the Lilapur police station area, worked as a contractual computer operator in the Supply Department. He was the youngest of three brothers. His elder brother Sushil Vishwakarma drives a taxi, while his other brother Sonu Vishwakarma is a farmer. According to the family complaint, Saurabh was returning home from the Supply Office in Lalganj between 7 pm and 7.15 pm on August 13. When he reached around 150 metres beyond Gajadhar Inter College, Saurabh Tiwari (32), Daroga Tiwari (30), Sonu Tiwari (30), Anuj Tiwari (32) and others surrounded him. The accused brutally assaulted him. Hearing Saurabh's cries for help, local residents reached the spot. They informed Saurabh's friends Sonu Upadhyay and Shubham Pandey about the incident. Both reached the spot and took Saurabh to the Medical College for treatment, where doctors declared him dead. As soon as the incident was reported, ASP Brijnandan Rai reached the spot with a police team and took details of the incident. Police have been deployed in the area in view of the tension. Read full news in chronological manner Before dying, he said: They hit me with a gun butt and broke my leg Before his death, the computer operator said, "Daroga Tiwari and the son of his brother Bade Tiwari, along with 8-10 people, beat me with sticks. They hit my neck with the butt of a gun and also broke my leg." Family says accused had opened fire at their house four months ago The family said Sanjay alias Bade Tiwari is the former block chief of Laxmanganj, while his brother Sonu Tiwari is a ration dealer. The accused allegedly developed a grudge after Saurabh refused to approve a ration card-related work for Sonu. Four months ago, the accused had also allegedly fired 6-7 rounds at their house. The family said Saurabh was killed because of this dispute. Father-in-law demands encounter of accused Saurabh's father-in-law, Sajjan Vishwakarma, said, "Our demand is that all the accused should be arrested. After their arrest, they should be killed in an encounter and their houses should be demolished with bulldozers. Saurabh's wife should be given a government job. The government should also provide financial assistance for his four-month-old daughter." Friends took him to the hospital Hearing Saurabh's screams after the attack, people from the vicinity reached the spot. They informed his friends Sonu Upadhyay and Shubham Pandey about the incident. Both reached the spot and took Saurabh to the medical college for treatment, where doctors declared him dead. A video from before Saurabh's death has also surfaced. In it, he has also named the accused and said- Daroga Tiwari and his brother Bade Tiwari's son, along with 8-10 people, assaulted me with sticks. They hit my neck with a rifle butt and also broke my leg. Firing at home four months ago Family members said that Sonu Tiwari, brother of former block head Bade Tiwari of Laxmanpur, who is a ration dealer. The accused had harbored enmity after Sonu's ration card work was not approved. About four months ago, the accused had also fired 6-7 rounds at their house. Due to this animosity, the accused have murdered Saurabh. Police force deployed, body sent for post-mortem Considering the tension in the area after the incident, police force was deployed. ASP Brijnandan Rai reached the spot with the police team and gathered information about the incident. The body was taken into custody and sent for post-mortem. Brijnandan Rai informed that a case has been registered based on Saurabh's complaint. It is a case of old enmity. The accused are being searched for. One accused, Daroga Tiwari, was arrested on Friday morning.

stories.title: Student reaches police outpost over no teaching at school:Says, 'Ma’am keeps using phone, what will happen to our future?'
stories.summary: In Kanpur Dehat, a 12-year-old seventh-grade student reached the police outpost with a complaint about not being taught. He told the outpost in-charge, "Teachers don't teach, they use their phones all day. Older students beat younger children, and children keep playing in the ground." He asked, What will happen to our future? The policemen were surprised to hear the student's words. A head constable took him to the school. In front of the police, the female teacher started scolding the student and threatened to beat him. The police explained to the teacher and advised her not to do so. The incident took place on August 10, around 12 noon. The video of the incident surfaced on Thursday. The student studies in the seventh grade at a government school in Rasdhan, about 30 km from the district headquarters. On the instructions of the BSA, a notice has been issued to the headmaster and the accused teacher. See pictures Know full story Sanjeev Mishra, a resident of Rasdhan, is a farmer. He has five children - four sons and one daughter. 12-year-old Madhav is the fourth child. He studies in the seventh grade at the government composite school in the village. On August 10, Madhav reached the Rasdhan police outpost in his school uniform. The policemen were surprised to see him. When asked the reason for coming to the outpost, he said that he had come to complain about his school. Madhav said that there is no studying in school. Teachers are busy using their phones. Children keep playing in the ground all day. Older students beat him up frequently. No action is taken even after complaining. I am very troubled. He said that when he left school for the outpost, the madam was still talking on the phone. After hearing the student's complaint, the head constable of the outpost took him to the school. In front of the police, the teacher threatened the student A conversation took place between the student and teacher Saima Khan in the presence of policemen at the school. The police asked the teacher about the student's complaint. During this, the teacher started scolding the student and threatening to hit him. The policemen made a video of the incident. Read conversation between the student and the teacher Teacher: Why did you go to the police? Whatever the problem is, tell me directly. Student: You don't listen. Who should I tell? Teacher: We don't listen? I will hit you so much right now, I will beat you until your mind is set straight. When the teacher flared up, policemen stopped her from talking to the child in that manner. After pacifying both of them, the policemen returned. Investigation on BSA's instructions, Notice to Headmaster and Teacher After the video surfaced, on the instructions of BSA Ashish Pandey, the Block Education Officer (BEO) reached the school and investigated. He spoke to students and school staff and submitted his report to the BSA. Based on the report, the BSA issued show-cause notices to Headmaster Anupam Kumar and teacher Saima Khan. Both have been summoned to the BSA office for clarification. According to the BEO, some students had beaten the complainant student. He went to the teacher to complain about it, but at that time the teacher was talking on the phone and did not listen to him. Annoyed by this, the student reached the police outpost. Outpost In-charge said - The complaint was about lack of studies Rasdhan Outpost In-charge Prashant Singh said- A child had come to the outpost with a complaint. The outpost's constable took him to school. The child was complaining about the lack of studies in school. The matter was not serious, but the way the teacher scolded the child in front of the police personnel was wrong. BSA said - There was a dispute among children Basic Education Officer Ashish Pandey said- There was a dispute among the children. The police post is right next to the school, so the child went there. The Block Education Officer went to the spot and investigated. The child's parents were also called to the school. According to them, the child becomes a bit aggressive. For now, he has been counselled.

stories.title: Auto driver's Son files murder FIR:Body found floating in Varuna River on 6 August; acid found in vehicle
stories.summary: On the night of August 6, 2026, an abandoned auto-rickshaw was found on the Varuna Bridge in the Cantt police station area of Varanasi. The auto-rickshaw number was UP65 ET8037. During the investigation, the police found the auto-rickshaw belonged to Gyanchand Sonkar, a resident of Ardali Bazar, Cantt police station. A bottle of acid was found in the auto-rickshaw. Upon searching, Gyanchand's body was found floating in the Varuna River below the bridge. In this regard, on the night of August 13, the police registered a murder case based on the complaint. The deceased's son, Satish Sonkar, filed a murder complaint with the Cantt police. Based on this, the police have registered a case and started action. Murder on 6 August Satish stated in the complaint given to the police, My father Gyanchand Sonkar used to drive his private auto-rickshaw. He had no enmity with anyone, nor did he have much to do with anyone at home. When he did not return home by 11 PM on the night of August 6, I called his number.When I called, the police answered the phone and asked who I was, so I explained everything, upon which they called me to the Varuna Bridge. Body found floating in Varuna Satish said, Upon reaching there, the auto was found abandoned, and a half-empty bottle of acid was found further ahead. After this, we and the police started searching for father. When searched in the Varuna river below, father's body was found floating there, upon which he was pulled out. Someone has murdered my father. In such a situation, a complaint has been lodged with the police today. In this regard, Cantt Police Station in-charge Raj Kishore Pandey said, Based on the complaint of the deceased Gyanchand's son, a case has been registered under BNS Section 103(1) and the search for the murderer is underway. He will be apprehended soon. Had said a constable was following On August 6, upon finding the body, Satish had said that father had been troubled for a long time and was repeatedly saying that a constable was following him. In such a situation, the police are also investigating that angle. Currently, the search for the murderer is being conducted using CCTV footage.

stories.title: CCTV shows doctor jumping to death from 8th floor:Note blames conwoman Garima; sister breaks down, daughter says, ‘Papa, come back’
stories.summary: A doctor in Gorakhpur died by suicide after jumping from the eighth floor of his apartment on Thursday. A CCTV camera captured his final moments, while a note found in his pocket named alleged fraudster Garima Singh and her gang as responsible for his death. Dr Paramatma Singh left his flat at around 9.10 am, went to the basement and took a lift to the eighth floor before reaching the terrace. He jumped from the building shortly afterwards. Residents took him to a nearby private hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Daughter returns from school, says ‘Papa, please come back’ Singh’s 12-year-old son Arihant and seven-year-old daughter Parnika, known as Binni, were called home from school after the incident. When Binni saw her father’s body, she broke down and repeatedly said, “Papa, please come back.” She later clung to her elder brother and cried. Singh’s wife, Dr Sumitra Singh, also works as a government veterinary doctor. His younger sister Ranjana Singh said Sumitra had called her two days earlier, telling her that Paramatma was under severe stress over a loan-related matter. Ranjana said she had planned to visit and speak to him but could not reach him in time. Post-mortem finds multiple fractures A post-mortem examination found multiple fractures and serious internal injuries. The report said his neck, ribs, legs, spine and arms had suffered fractures. His body was taken to his ancestral home in Mau after the post-mortem. His last rites are scheduled for Friday. Who is Garima Singh? According to the police, Garima Singh, who holds a PhD, allegedly ran a loan fraud operation with her father Dhruv Narayan Singh and others. Police said she targeted railway officials, doctors and teachers by promising to arrange loans or help them close existing loans. Four cases have been registered against her so far this month, while six more complaints have been received. Police allege that around ₹10 crore may have been taken from 10 people. Garima and her father have been in jail since August 3. Seven days before his death, Dr Paramatma Singh had filed a complaint alleging that Garima had cheated him of ₹1.40 crore. Doctor allegedly took loans from six banks According to the complaint, Garima contacted Singh in February 2026 through a relative. She allegedly claimed that she could help close his existing home loan through a new personal loan. Police allege that Singh was made to take loans from six banks and transfer the money to accounts linked to Garima. She initially paid two instalments but later allegedly stopped making payments and threatened his family. FIR filed against Garima and associates Based on a complaint by Singh’s cousin Dileep Singh, Gorakhnath police registered a case of abetment of suicide against Garima Singh and her alleged associates on Thursday evening. Police may question Garima in jail as part of the investigation. SSP Dr Kaustubh said police would also invoke the Gangsters Act against Garima and other members of the alleged gang. Their financial activities are being investigated, and police are examining their bank accounts and properties allegedly linked to the fraud. Paramatma Singh, originally from Mau, had settled in Gorakhpur several years ago. He lived with his wife and two children in a two-bedroom flat at Basant Enclave in Rajendra Nagar. He was posted as a government veterinary doctor in Nautanwa, Maharajganj, while his wife was posted in the Siswan block of the same district.

stories.title: 'He called me his daughter, we only took a photo':Sister denies any relationship with Mahant; 2 friends buried in Baghpat temple
stories.summary: My brother left home on the 25th. Everyone searched for him a lot, but he was not found anywhere. Today it was revealed that he was killed and buried in the Ganesh temple. I have no relation with the Mahant. He used to say that I consider you my daughter. He had taken a photo with me in Haridwar, but I have no connection with him. This is what Ankit's sister said, who is rumored to be having an affair with the Mahant. In Baghpat, Mahant Naresh Nath of Ganesh Temple killed and buried 2 friends, then plastered over it and installed tiles. On Thursday (August 13), the police arrested 2 disciples of the Mahant. One disciple made several revelations in his confession. The case is from the Chandinagar police station area, 20 km away from the district headquarters. Know the full case In Sigoli Taga village, Ankit (25) lived with his mother and 5 sisters. He was the only son of the house. 2 sisters are married. Ankit was unmarried and unemployed. Israr's (32) house is right in front of his house. Israr used to support his family by working as a laborer. His family includes his wife Firdaus and 3 children. On the afternoon of July 25, Ankit and Israr left on a bike. When both did not return until the next day, their family members started looking for them. But, nothing was known about either of them. Calls were made to both their phones, but the mobiles were not picked up. From the evening of July 27, both their mobiles were switched off. Missing person report filed 4 days later On July 29, a missing person report was filed at Chandinagar police station. When both did not return even after 8-10 days, the police became active. The police checked call details, last known locations, and questioned villagers. In this, the name of Mahant Naresh Nath of Ganesh Temple located in Lahchaura came to light. Both were last seen near the Ganesh Temple. The police also learned about an affair between the Mahant and Ankit's sister. Accused Mahant absconded upon getting a hint Police raided the temple on Wednesday (August 12) night, but Mahant Naresh Nath (40) got wind of it and fled. Police found his disciple Ujjwal in the temple. Initially, he tried to mislead the police, but broke down under strict interrogation. Later, police also arrested another disciple, Krishna Yadav. Now read the confession of accused Ujjwal Ujjwal told the police - On August 25, Ankit and Israr came to the ashram very angrily. At that time, Mahant Naresh Nath, his 14-year-old son, I, and Krishna Yadav were present in the ashram. The Mahant calmed Ankit and Israr. He said that I will solve your problem, but first, have tea as prasad. Mixed intoxicant in tea and gave it to them The Mahant had already mixed an intoxicating substance in that tea, which made both of them unconscious as soon as they drank it. After that, the Mahant took out a poisonous injection from his car and administered it to both of them. When I asked that they would die, the Mahant told us to remain silent. Engaged minor son in watch duty Naresh Nath had told me that I charge 40 thousand for performing a marriage, but I will get your marriage done for free. Meanwhile, Krishna Yadav was lured with the promise that I would teach him tantra vidya (occult knowledge). After this, Krishna and I together dug a 6-foot deep pit. The Mahant's 14-year-old son had also come to the ashram. He was made to stand at the gate for watch duty. Phone thrown 10 km away to mislead Upon their death, they were buried in a pit. Tiles were installed over that pit. To mislead the police, Israr's phone was thrown 10 kilometers away in the jungle. When the police removed the tiles, the decomposed bodies of Ankit and Israr were found. They were identified by their clothes and watches. The bike Ankit and Israr used to reach Ganesh Temple has not yet been recovered. Sister was living at her maternal home after marriage One of Ankit's sisters had come to live at her maternal home after marriage. Earlier, the mahant used to live in Ankit's neighborhood and performed worship. However, his conduct was not good. Because of this, the villagers had expelled him from the village. After this, he started living with his two disciples at Ganesh Temple, 2 km away from the village. There had been fights many times before It is believed that Ankit and Israr had gone to convince the Mahant regarding his affair with their sister. There had been fights over this many times before. When the sister was asked about her affair with the Mahant, she denied it. The sister says that the Mahant used to call her his daughter. She had no relationship with him. A month and a half ago, we went to Haridwar with our family. The Mahant told me that I was like his daughter. During that time, he took a photo with me. All the talks about an affair are just rumors. I have no relationship with him. Baghpat SP Suraj Rai said that The dead bodies of both youths have been recovered from the temple. The Mahant's disciples, Ujjwal and Krishna, have been arrested. The search for the Mahant and his son has been intensified. 6 police teams are involved. The accused Mahant is originally from Uttarakhand. A police team has also been dispatched to Uttarakhand.

stories.title: How big an issue will Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway be in UP?:SP highlights Agra, BSP touts Yamuna Expressway; how will BJP counter?
stories.summary: Since its inauguration on 13 July, the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway has been sinking somewhere or the other every day. In a month, more than 100 instances of sinking have been reported. The opposition is continuously making it an issue. Akhilesh Yadav is highlighting the features of the Agra Expressway from his time, and Akash Anand is praising the Yamuna Expressway from the BSP era. At the same time, questions are also being raised about the quality of Purvanchal Expressway, Ganga Expressway, and Gorakhpur Link Expressway. Meanwhile, the BJP government, which boasts of building the most expressways in UP, is on the back foot. In today's UP Explainer, find out if the opposition will be able to capitalise on this issue in the assembly elections and draw votes to its side? How will the BJP avoid this damage? Why is the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway sinking repeatedly? Is this the most sinking expressway till date? Yes, in terms of scale and duration, this is the most sinking expressway. However, the government or NHAI has not officially stated this. But, based on the number and duration of incidents recorded in media reports, this is the picture that emerges What loss will the BJP suffer due to the poor construction of the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway? Political experts say that this has dealt a blow to BJP's development model and good governance image. Even before this, the issue of poor construction of several expressways in UP has been raised, but there were no elections then. So everything was managed. But, it doesn't seem to be happening here. This can be understood as follows How big an issue will the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway become in the elections? Political analysts are divided on this. Some talk about its widespread impact. Meanwhile, some experts say that this issue will cool down by the elections. How important are expressways for the development of a state? Expressways are considered the lifeline of development for any state or country. This can be understood in 2 points

stories.title: Farrukhabad-Budaun highway submerged, barricades installed:44,000 people from 62 villages forced to leave their homes; evacuation announcement made
stories.summary: After the surge in the Ganga river, the Farrukhabad-Badaun highway has been submerged. At two places, two to three feet of water has accumulated for 100 to 150 meters. Traffic has been stopped by putting up barricades. Due to the flood, more than 44 thousand people from 62 villages have been forced to leave their homes. Floodwater has started reaching some of the relief camps that were set up. Children and women have been sent to other camps. The Ganga river is continuously eroding its banks. It is flowing 1.5 km away from its original course. As a result, 32 houses have collapsed so far. Seeing the deteriorating situation, NDRF (National Disaster Response Force) has been called in. PAC personnel are transporting people stranded in the water to safe places with the help of boats and steamers. Having to travel 14 km extra to go to Badaun Among the villages in Farrukhabad that are affected by floods, the highest number, 27 villages, are in Amritpur tehsil. The people there say - 'This is the sign of Amritpur, water on both sides of the road.' Every year, as the water level of the Ganga rises, this road is bound to get submerged. In 2025, the State Highway remained blocked for 15 days. Until now, vehicles going from Farrukhabad to Badaun used to go via Rajepur Tiraaha to Badaun. However, currently, the State Highway near Chitrakoot village has been submerged. Police duty has been assigned on the highway to prevent people from going onto the submerged road. Police are diverting vehicles from the Dabra area towards Badaun. People have to travel about 14 km extra. No shelter in relief camps, they are living on house roofs Chitrakoot village is near the State Highway. The entire village is submerged. We met Rajpal amidst the water. He says - the village is filled with water all around. There is also a risk of snakes and scorpions. People have to commute through these paths. A relief camp has been set up near the village. Only 10 to 20 people come here, because only that many names have been registered. Many people's names were not registered. They are forced to live on the roofs of their houses, waiting for the water to recede. Some have gone to their relatives' homes. This situation has persisted for 10 days. Last year's flood lasted for 30 days. Lost homes, set up tents by the roadside, then removed from there too Sukhdev, standing near us, says- Many houses in the village were submerged. Distressed people started living in tents by the roadside. Just 2-3 days ago, the administration announced (by beating drums) that this place is also dangerous and must be vacated. People were asked to go to relief camps. Those who are trapped on the roofs of their houses are not even getting clean drinking water. Ration and water are being delivered by boat, but the fear persists. People are somehow making ends meet. Tehsildar flared up when asked about water filling in the camp To understand the atmosphere of the relief camp, we reached the Pharmacy College in Chitrakoot village. The relief camp was set up here. The government school in the village was flooded. Because of this, a part of the school was also running in a section of the relief camp. Water has slowly started filling up outside the relief camp as well. SDM Shweta Sahu and Tehsildar Shashank Singh had arrived here. We asked the Tehsildar - "Floodwater has started filling up here, what are the preparations?" He angrily said - "Those who come to the camp will stay inside or will they roam outside? There is no water inside, is there?" We asked - "They will go outside for other needs." The Tehsildar said - "You tell us what we should do, because we don't know anything." Ration dealer said - A dam was built after 14 years, but it didn't even last a few months 12 villages in Farrukhabad Sadar Tehsil are flooded. Due to erosion in Rampur Dafarpur, several houses were swallowed by the river. On the boat going towards this village, the village's ration dealer, Subhash Chandra, was met. He says - Since 2012, it happens every year that after the water level in the Ganga rises, floods occur. People asked officials to build a dam so that the entire village could be saved from erosion. The Irrigation Department built a dam, but it didn't even last a few months. Some grain was sent by the government, which is being distributed among the people trapped in the flood. 'One house washed away, the other is saved so we are demolishing it' About 50 meters away from the strong current of the Ganga river, Meerawati was getting the debris of her broken house loaded onto a boat with her relatives. She says - We had an old house in this village. It was submerged in the river just 4 days ago. We were building another house here, but now this one is also going to be submerged. We are demolishing it and taking the bricks. Everyone here is troubled. Food and drink are not available. We have lost everything from our farm to our home. Now we don't understand where to go? House filled with water, cows and goats are on the road 56-year-old Jabar Singh lived his entire life in the village and did farming. He says - we have cows and goats, the house is submerged in water. The animals are on the road. The fields are also flooded. Now, when the water recedes, we will return. We will rebuild our house here again. Every year there is a flood, and there is a lot of talk about help, but the truth is that people like us don't even get a penny. Who does the administration help, I wonder? Santosh from Madaiya village says, In our area, it's not just the problem of floods, the current of the Ganga is also eroding the land. Last year, the situation was very terrible. The entire Prithvipur village was eroded. These people did build a dam. But, it could not withstand the current of the Ganga. People are distressed, they are just surviving. 3 situations of flood, see in pictures 1. Erosion of Ganga river People are demolishing their houses themselves Crops submerged

In 1970s, Marty Bluewater bought land on island planned for 800 homes; he is now its only resident
stories.summary: Protection Island in Washington was once planned as a holiday community with 800 homes. Marty Bluewater bought a piece of the island in the 1970s, but conservationists later fought to protect its important wildlife habitat. In 1982, the entire 400-acre island became a National Wildlife Refuge. Bluewater was allowed to stay and eventually became its only human resident.

Currently in pretrial confinement, Watson's refusal to wear his military uniform led to this latest arrest. This incident follows his earlier detention on the Capitol steps for expressing political opinions, showcasing his awareness of the repercussions he faces for his stance.

stories.title: Panic in Amethi as 29 copper spheres emerge from ground during house construction; Archaeology (ASI) team examines suspected ammunition
stories.summary: During construction work in Bhanauli village, workers discovered twenty-nine large metal spheres buried deep within the ground. These intriguing copper spheres, each measuring sixty centimeters across, resembled ancient munitions. Local police and the Uttar Pradesh Archaeology Department quickly secured the unusual find. Specialists are now engaged in examining the spheres to determine their historical significance and origin, with plans for additional archaeological research to ascertain their context.

The discussions focused on crucial matters such as water sharing and infrastructure advancements. This council acts as a vital forum for fostering dialogue between state governments and the Centre, demonstrating a commitment to cooperative federalism and effective dispute resolution.

Oldest evidence of life on Earth has been discovered in India in a 3.4 billion-year-old layered rock shows signs of microbial life
stories.summary: Recent discoveries in India have unveiled biological traces that date back approximately 3.5 billion years, indicating a significantly ancient origin of life on Earth. Researchers have confirmed the presence of photosynthetic activity and intricate metabolic processes within these samples, which originated from environments close to underwater hydrothermal vents. This remarkable finding represents the oldest known biological materials found in rock formations.

Delays in appointing subsidiary body chairs affect Council effectiveness and credibility. Elected members seek more involvement in key UN processes. The Council's structure needs to reflect global changes since 1945.

Pulitzer Prize-winning poet bought a barren land in Hawaii and turned it into a 19-acre forest with more than 3,000 palms
stories.summary: W.S. Merwin, a celebrated poet, found solace and seclusion in Maui during the 1970s, where he dedicated himself to creating a lush 19-acre palm forest. This extraordinary project transformed a barren piece of land into a thriving ecological haven, showcasing an impressive array of palm species. Today, the Merwin Conservancy diligently safeguards this rich environmental legacy, ensuring it remains a vital part of our natural heritage.

stories.summary: The Supreme Court has mandated that the Centre set up specialized clinics for captive elephants, ensuring they receive essential periodic health checkups. Additionally, the ruling requires DNA mapping of each captive elephant to combat illegal trade. The court emphasizes the importance of maintaining these animals' welfare, instructing states to complete DNA profiling to thwart unlawful commercial activities and transfers.

stories.summary: In a remarkable discovery, a four-year-old boy stumbled upon a 16th-century gold pendant while metal detecting alongside his father in Essex. This exquisite relic, weighing just 8.68 grams and thought to contain a religious artifact, has been identified as a treasure trove. Valued at an astounding £2.5 million, this find provides fascinating insights into the religious practices and craftsmanship of the 1500s.

stories.title: Valkyrae Defends Thumbnail Artist: streamer says Uncharted art is not AI; warns on artists’ jobs
stories.summary: Valkyrae has addressed AI allegations surrounding her YouTube thumbnails after viewers accused her latest Uncharted artwork of being AI-generated. She defended her longtime artist, Anko, explaining that he creates her livestream thumbnails and regularly shares his creative process. Valkyrae said she understands why people may suspect AI but stressed, “But it’s not AI.” She also expressed concern about AI threatening artists’ jobs and livelihoods.

In Peter Santenello’s exploration, longtime residents recall lost jobs, stability and a shared way of life, while local businesses and tourism offer hope. As the town seeks new industry, its resilient residents remain determined to rebuild.

Following court directives, Roy presented himself to the investigation officer but chose not to respond to the questions asked by the authorities. The court had previously granted him interim pre-arrest bail, providing some protection amidst this legal turmoil.

82-year-old Tony Fahey builds ‘walking on water’ machine for charity record
stories.summary: At 82, Tony Fahey embarks on a daring 24-hour world record attempt on water using a unique human-powered vessel named the aqua elliptica. This remarkable challenge seeks to generate funds for Make-A-Wish UK, reflecting his commitment to supporting children with serious health conditions. Following a serious accident years ago, Fahey returns to the water to showcase his remarkable endurance and innovative spirit.

stories.summary: A talented high school student has pioneered a cutting-edge bioengineering method for the early detection of pancreatic cancer. By utilizing magnetic beads to isolate tumor-derived particles from blood samples, her clinical trials demonstrated remarkable accuracy. Her extraordinary research has secured her a spot as a national finalist in a prestigious science competition, offering a promising new avenue for timely diagnosis and improved patient survival outcomes.

In 1961, British scientists stopped farming a 4-hectare barley field and left it alone; 60 years later...
stories.summary: A groundbreaking six-decade study reveals that passive rewilding effectively fosters the development of lush native woodlands. Through protective thorny scrub, young trees thrived, shielded from herbivores, while wind and jays ingeniously spread seeds, outlining the woodlands’ unique patterns. After fifty years, the area began to mirror the characteristics of ancient woodlands, showcasing an eco-friendly and budget-friendly approach to achieving woodland restoration objectives.

In 1963, a California builder made a house that rotates 320 degrees using two washing-machine motors
stories.summary: A remarkable rotating house, built in 1963 by the imaginative Sam Harkleroad, is now available for sale, showcasing a one-of-a-kind design. Overlooking busy Highway 101, this property comprises seven homes, all presently leased, with a total price tag of $3.3 million. Harkleroad's distinctive architectural legacy thrives across Marin County, but his grandson has chosen to list the asset, citing the complexities of maintenance as a challenge.

stories.title: Giant 746lb bluefin tuna caught off Yorkshire after nearly 90 years as scientists explain UK return
stories.summary: A giant 746lb (338kg) Atlantic bluefin tuna has been caught off the Yorkshire coast, around 10 miles from Whitby, after nearly 90 years. Scientists say warming seas, recovering fish stocks and tighter fishing controls may be behind the species’ return. The catch comes near Whitby, where an 851lb British record was set in 1933.

Man and his dog uncover a 3,400-year-old Bronze Age axe in England
stories.summary: In an English forest, a fortunate man and his dog uncovered an astonishing 3,400-year-old axe head emblematic of Britain's Bronze Age. This remarkable find sheds light on the enduring mysteries of our ancient past, revealing the metalworking capabilities of prehistoric communities. Artifacts like this one remind us that hidden treasures await discovery in even the most familiar settings.

stories.title: Missouri engineer hand-built an underground home into a hillside; 50yrs later, it remains leak-free
stories.summary: A Missouri engineer spent years carving an underground home into an Ozarks hillside, building it largely by hand without an architect. Designed to resemble a natural cave, the property features steel-reinforced concrete, an earth-based ventilation system, heavy oak beams and railroad-inspired details. His son Zane now restores the remarkable 50-year-old home and surrounding 225-acre property.

Meet Natalie Muro, 18-year-old Colorado student who used an invasive plant to fight algal blooms
stories.summary: A remarkable eighteen-year-old student has developed an ingenious device aimed at eradicating toxic algal blooms. Utilizing wind-driven waves and invasive plant species, this unique system demonstrated impressive results in field tests, removing nearly all cyanobacteria and trapping decayed cell matter. This groundbreaking solution offers a cost-effective way to restore and revitalize unhealthy freshwater ecosystems.

stories.title: Amit Shah to chair meeting with CMs, top officials of southern states to resolve inter-state issues
stories.summary: In Mahabalipuram, Home Minister Amit Shah will oversee the Southern Zonal Council meeting, where crucial discussions about water sharing and education priorities among states will take place. Following this, he is set to travel to Siliguri to inaugurate new border security projects, and engage with personnel from Sashastra Seema Bal. His visit will wrap up with a comprehensive review meeting on border security.

stories.title: 1958, the US secretly detonated 3 nuclear devices 100–500 km above the South Atlantic
stories.summary: In a clandestine effort, Operation Argus conducted nuclear tests in the stratosphere over the South Atlantic Ocean. These detonations resulted in spectacular artificial auroras and fleeting radiation belts around our planet. The mission’s intent was to shield against Soviet missile threats and radar detection systems. Yet, the swift vanishing of these barriers caused significant communication disturbances, leading to the formulation of international accords banning nuclear experiments in space.

stories.title: Scientists simulate nuclear strike to stop a 160-metre asteroid impact
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking study, scientists conducted simulations showcasing the potential of nuclear warheads to neutralize hazardous asteroids. These experiments focused on strategies for fragmenting large asteroids prior to their collision with Earth. While this approach holds promise for planetary protection, it is viewed as a last resort, especially for threats detected late. Ongoing research is crucial for insights into fragment dynamics and their long-lasting consequences.

In the 1970s, a New Mexico architect built Earthships from tyres and cans for extreme weather
stories.summary: Michael Reynolds pioneered the Earthship concept, creating innovative homes constructed from repurposed materials that encourage self-sufficiency. These structures harness recycled resources and natural systems for energy and water usage. Earthships serve as a robust solution against infrastructure breakdowns and natural calamities. This approach is now shaping a wider trend in sustainable construction practices, showcasing an off-grid living model.

The government has promoted higher ethanol blending as a way to reduce crude oil imports, save foreign exchange and improve India's energy security. India also achieved its 20% blending target ahead of the original 2030 deadline. However, the nationwide shift has generated concerns among some vehicle owners, particularly those with older vehicles.

4,000-year-old painted stone in Indonesia reveals art carried by ancient Austronesian voyagers
stories.summary: A painted stone found on Indonesia's Wetar Island offers ancient insights. This artifact dates back over 4,000 years and shows early artistic traditions. The artwork predates Neolithic pottery, revealing a significant cultural development. Portable symbols likely traveled with Austronesian voyagers across islands. This discovery reshapes our understanding of ancient maritime cultural exchanges.

Two Mumbai doctors to receive Pakistan’s highest civilian honour for keeping Jinnah’s illness secret
stories.summary: In a remarkable recognition, two Parsi physicians have been nominated posthumously for Pakistan's prestigious civilian award. They upheld the confidentiality surrounding Muhammad Ali Jinnah's terminal health condition prior to Partition, demonstrating a silent commitment to their professional ethics. This discreet dedication played an inadvertent yet significant role in the formation of Pakistan. The award ceremony is scheduled for March 2027.

stories.title: Destroyed by a 2015 storm, a Virginia refuge beach lot is now moving 2.5 miles north
stories.summary: Chincoteague National Wildlife Refuge is relocating its beach facilities to a more secure northern position following significant storm damage. This proactive approach not only aims to cut future repair costs but also accommodates the natural shifts of the island. While new parking arrangements will be established, the former site will transition back into its native ecosystem.

Modi govt's Gen Z outreach: One Union minister to visit one university every day
stories.summary: The proposed initiative, called 'One Day, One University', is aimed at strengthening the government's engagement with young people. During these visits, ministers are expected to hold discussions with students, hear their views on issues affecting the country and explain government schemes meant for students and young people. The plan comes at a time when student protests over the NEET paper leak issue have intensified in parts of the country.

stories.title: At 14, Sheri Lynch got a grey hippo; 40 years later, she had 1,086 items
stories.summary: Sheri Lynch has achieved Guinness World Records fame for her extraordinary hippo collection, which began with a single plush toy gifted to her in her teenage years. Over the span of more than forty years, she has gathered more than a thousand hippo-themed treasures from various corners of the globe.

Bought in 2016, Indiana bishop’s former home with chapel is now listed at $1.28 million
stories.summary: After nine years of dedication, an Indiana family has lovingly restored a historic home that once served as a Catholic bishop's residence, complete with a private chapel. Purchased at auction in 2016, they meticulously preserved its original features and completed extensive renovations. Now listed for $1.284 million, the family is ready to embark on new adventures and explore the world.

stories.title: European wild boars escaped a North Carolina hunting ranch in 1912; a century later...
stories.summary: Invasive European wild boars, originally introduced to the area in 1912, are wreaking havoc within Great Smoky Mountains National Park. To mitigate damage to delicate ecosystems, park management annually removes around 275 of these feral hogs. The boars breed with domestic pigs, creating hybrid species that further disrupt native wildlife. Efforts to control their population involve trapping, shooting, and implementing fencing strategies.

stories.title: Sumit Sarkar: The Citizen Historian
stories.summary: Professor Sumit Sarkar significantly impacted the understanding of Indian nationalism, illuminating its intricacies through comprehensive analysis. He explored the evolution of nationalism, internal disputes, and collective movements, while challenging conventional binaries. His focus on ordinary people's cravings for justice defined his contributions as a public thinker and citizen historian. This article pays tribute to his influential teaching and the lasting academic heritage he leaves behind.

stories.title: FSSAI action prompts Amway, Emami, four other brands to drop '100%' product claims
stories.summary: FSSAI said Bonn Biscuits had used a "100%" claim in an for its Bonn Cummin Flavor Jeera Bite Biscuits, 76 gm. The company has since removed the claim from its website. Emami was also asked to address its use of a 100 per cent claim for Zhandu Honey. According to FSSAI, the company complied with its advisory and took corrective action.
