A British duke sent six Himalayan tahr to New Zealand in 1904; five survived the voyage, and...
stories.summary: Himalayan tahr were introduced to New Zealand's South Island by British aristocrats in pursuit of sport hunting back in 1904. Quickly multiplying, these creatures turned into an invasive species, wreaking havoc on native alpine ecosystems. Control measures, including government-led aerial shooting, have not proven entirely effective, creating a challenging situation for conservationists and hunters alike. The management of tahr remains an ongoing struggle within New Zealand's wildlife strategy.

stories.title: Young YouTuber Buys NYC Apartment: Eden Masliah mixes savings and inheritance; questions feeling fully proud
stories.summary: YouTuber Eden Masliah, 21, has purchased a $740,000 two-bedroom N.Y.C. apartment after saving about $250,000 from her content career and using money left by her late father for an investment. Although the purchase marks a major milestone, Masliah admits she struggles to see it as entirely her achievement because of her inheritance. She is now renovating the apartment and hopes to create a timeless space that reflects her personal style.

3 killed, 3 injured after truck gas tank explodes at Delhi CNG station while refuelling
stories.summary: A fire service officer said all six injured people were taken to hospital, where they were receiving treatment. Further information about the rest three is awaited. Fire service personnel also took precautionary measures at the station and worked to bring the situation under control. The cause of the explosion has not yet been established. An investigation is underway to determine what led to the gas tank bursting.

stories.title: Amidst the AI data centre backlash, a Missouri farmer is inviting developers to buy his land
stories.summary: In Missouri, a farmer has taken the unexpected step of inviting data center developers to bid on his land, despite notable local opposition and recent state restrictions. He believes that data centers could revitalize struggling rural economies by creating jobs and generating tax revenue. The farmer also addresses valid concerns about water use and electricity costs, presenting his offer as an opportunity for growth even when local prospects are dim.

stories.summary: Witch Island, previously inhabited by the infamous Anna Chittenden—referred to as the 'Witch of Wall Street'—has transformed into a wildlife sanctuary. After her brief stay, Jane Sewall took on the responsibility of safeguarding the isle from irresponsible tourists. In 1986, Sewall gifted the island to the Maine Audubon Society, which is now overseen by the Coastal Rivers Conservation Trust.

stories.summary: Tragedy struck when TikTok sensation Ayesha Gilamana, popularly known as Shamsu Bibi, was shot and killed while driving. Assailants on a motorcycle opened fire, leading to a crash involving her vehicle. Ayesha's younger sister was injured in the wreck and is now receiving treatment. Authorities have arrested three suspects believed to be related to the attackers, as investigations continue to uncover the motive behind this shocking incident.

stories.title: Congress may move court if Pune curfew blocks Rahul Gandhi’s ‘Chhatron ki Goonj’ event
stories.summary: Congress may approach courts if Pune administration halts Rahul Gandhi's student convention. The party secured college permission for the August 22 event, facing a fortnight's gathering ban. This ban, imposed for protests and festivals, is seen as targeting the Congress program. Previous attempts to block similar conventions occurred in Dehradun, Allahabad, and Kota. The party believes the BJP is attempting to disrupt its youth outreach efforts.

stories.title: In 1943, Franklin Delano Roosevelt gave Springwood and 33 acres to US; estate had 1,500 acres and 500,000 trees
stories.summary: President Franklin D. Roosevelt generously bequeathed his family's Springwood estate to the government, substantially enhancing the property throughout his life. By planting over 500,000 trees, Roosevelt transformed the surrounding landscape. This pivotal donation secured the lasting preservation of this notable presidential site, which became both America’s first presidential library and a cherished national historic landmark.

stories.title: FBI puts Indian national Major Singh on Most Wanted list
Meet Kanav Jain: Scottish student who built a low-cost autonomous aircraft to deliver medicines to remote communities
stories.summary: Kanav Jain, a talented Scottish student, has been awarded the prestigious UK Young Engineer of the Year for creating AeroAid, an innovative low-cost autonomous drone aimed at delivering medical supplies. This versatile VTOL quadplane combines the best features of helicopters and airplanes, making it ideal for reaching remote locations. Jain’s mission is to leverage technology for vital humanitarian assistance, reflecting his commitment as a leader in drone technology workshops.

Between 1969 and 1972, US released a weevil to fight musk thistle; it later attacked native thistles
stories.summary: A biological control initiative aimed at managing invasive thistles integrated a weevil specifically targeting musk thistle. Unfortunately, this insect extended its reach to native plant species, leading to detrimental effects on local thistles, including an endangered variety that experienced a decline in seed production. This situation underscores the critical importance of careful evaluation in invasive species control programs.

stories.title: Disney built Disneyland around a family farm that refused a $90 million offer
stories.summary: For decades, the Fujishige family refused to sell their 58-acre farm in Anaheim, even as Disneyland and surrounding development transformed the area. Disney and other developers made repeated offers for the valuable land, but the family continued growing strawberries and vegetables. After years of pressure and a bitter fight with the city, the family finally agreed to sell in 1998, shortly before Hiroshi Fujishige died. The former farm later became the Toy Story parking lot at Disneyland.

stories.title: A 2,500-year-old sacred well in Italy hid bronze offerings and two human skeletons
stories.summary: Archaeologists found an unusual ritual well at ancient Etruscan city Kainua in Italy. Two bronze statuettes and a rare bronze plate were discovered at the well's bottom. These objects were votive offerings placed during a foundation ritual centuries ago. Two adult human skeletons were also found, marking the structure's ritual closing. The findings offer new insights into Etruscan city foundations and religious traditions.

stories.title: Australian couple bought a cattle farm and planted 34,000 trees to restore rainforest

Netanyahu's party puts Mamdani alongside Iran, Hezbollah leaders on billboard

Netanyahu is campaigning for re-election amid political challenges in Israel. He has increasingly used Mamdani's criticism as campaign messaging. The exchange occurs while Gaza ceasefire efforts remain stalled.

stories.summary: Kandersteg village in Switzerland faces a significant landslide threat from an unstable mountain. Scientists link this danger to thawing permafrost and changing glacier dynamics caused by climate change. While the threat is not immediate, authorities have prepared evacuation plans and monitoring systems. Residents are aware of the risks but remain calm, trusting the implemented safety measures. This situation highlights the increasing natural risks faced by mountain communities globally.

stories.title: Kansas couple builds tornado-resistant home from tyres, cans and boxes
stories.summary: In an innovative twist on sustainable living, a couple in Kansas is transforming discarded items into a unique residence. This Earthship features around 1,000 tires and 16,000 aluminum cans, built to endure severe weather, including tornadoes and fires. It will autonomously generate power, harvest rainwater, and process wastewater, demonstrating how waste can be creatively repurposed into a haven.

stories.title: 'Foolproof system in place, difficult to breach': Centre lists NEET exam security measures before SC
In 1993, an art historian found a forgotten painting; 33 years later, its female creator was rediscovered
stories.summary: A remarkable find by an art historian in 1993 ignited a relentless pursuit to recover the lost masterpieces of Michaelina Wautier. This accomplished 17th-century painter's works had long been misattributed to men throughout history. The pivotal recovery of her 'The Five Senses' series in 2020 heralded a new era, culminating in a landmark exhibition at London's Royal Academy in 2026, finally restoring her rightful legacy after centuries in the shadows.

stories.title: A rotating 'garbage island' spreads over 1.6 million sq km in the Pacific with 50 kilograms of plastic per square kilometre
stories.summary: Between the shores of Hawaii and California floats a staggering 1.6 million square kilometers of plastic debris. This island of waste includes not just nets and ropes but also countless microplastics that pose serious threats to marine wildlife. Animals often mistake plastics for food, while others become trapped in ghost fishing gear.

stories.title: Vijay govt revokes order barring students from Left, CJP protests in Tamil Nadu
'Voice sample is not required': Rahul Gandhi’s counsel opposes plea in Savarkar defamation case
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi's lawyer opposed a plea for his voice sample in a defamation case. The defense argued the request was premature for the ongoing court proceedings. Satyaki Savarkar's deposition also brought Godse-RSS links into focus during cross-examination. The defamation case stems from remarks made by Rahul in London during 2023. The court has directed the defense to file its formal response by September 1.

'We need to meet': Envoy says PM Modi wants Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman's visit to be 'memorable'
stories.summary: India's High Commissioner emphasized Prime Minister Modi's desire for a memorable visit. He assured Prime Minister Rahman of an appropriate and honorable reception. This engagement aims to benefit people and businesses in both nations. India calls for trust and dialogue to address current bilateral differences. Both countries should build on shared history and aspirations for future prosperity.

stories.summary: Noreen Niazi met her brother Imran Khan in Adiala Jail after nine months. The Supreme Court ordered weekly family meetings and his transfer to a hospital. Imran also met his wife, Bushra Bibi, for a longer duration. Medical reports indicated fluctuating blood pressure and anxiety for the former prime minister. The court stressed family access as a fundamental right, not a concession.

Jharkhand govt releases list of 44 recruitment exams cancelled over irregularities
stories.summary: The government said the cancellations followed "complaints regarding irregularities in ongoing examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and executed through TDPL, and based on facts brought before the government during the CID investigation."

stories.title: Democrat Angie Nixon defeats Alexander Vindman in surprise Florida Senate primary upset
stories.summary: Angie Nixon secured a surprise Democratic Senate primary victory in Florida. She will now face Republican Ashley Moody in the general election. Byron Donalds and David Jolly won their respective governor primary nominations. New congressional maps are expected to favor Republicans significantly. These primaries set the stage for Florida's November political direction.

stories.title: US vs ICC row escalates: Trump administration sanctions international court president, senior lawyer
stories.summary: In a significant escalation against the International Criminal Court (ICC), the United States has imposed sanctions on two prominent officials, including the ICC president and a senior trial lawyer. This move marks a continuation of the Trump administration's contentious stance towards the internationally recognized tribunal. The ICC criticized these sanctions as detrimental to the global legal framework, while several European allies voiced their concern over the U.S. actions.

stories.title: In 1831, the Blackburns fled slavery; 154 years later, their home was found
IShowSpeed Eyes WWE Return: Streamer teases comeback on livestream; Logan Paul feud looms
stories.summary: IShowSpeed has fueled speculation about another WWE appearance after teasing a return "very soon" during a recent livestream. The streamer last appeared at WrestleMania 42, teaming with Logan Paul and Austin Theory against The Usos and LA Knight. After their defeat, Paul turned on Speed, leading to a dramatic response when Speed drove him through an announce table. His latest tease could potentially set up another WWE storyline or renewed rivalry with Paul.

stories.title: Streamer Confirms She Is Alive: JollyIRL says she’s hurt after bungee jump; fans reflect on stunt risks
stories.summary: JollyIRL sparked widespread concern after her bungee jump livestream in Pattaya, Thailand, suddenly ended following a loud scream. The abrupt cutoff left viewers fearing she may have suffered a serious accident. The Kick streamer later confirmed she was alive and said her arm and neck were hurting, with possible whiplash. Fans expressed relief and discussed the risks of bungee jumping, while fellow streamer Sneako also voiced concern after watching the viral clip.

Owens And Wilson Clash: Misogynistic slur ignites Kirk case debate; fractures conservative media
stories.summary: Candace Owens and Andrew Wilson clashed during a heated three-hour PBD Podcast debate over Charlie Kirk’s assassination and the case against Tyler Robinson. Owens questioned evidence and investigative details while Wilson defended the prosecution’s case. The discussion became more contentious when Owens brought up Wilson’s previous comment about Erika Kirk, Charlie Kirk’s widow. Wilson then made a sweeping and offensive remark about women, intensifying criticism surrounding the debate and its participants.

To ensure quality, a rigorous four-tier reviewing system will be introduced to meticulously evaluate every examination paper. This reform comes on the heels of notable mistakes discovered in recent assessments. Additionally, the agency is welcoming fresh personnel and relocating its offices while implementing enhanced security measures and a thorough audit process.

stories.title: Captain of ship attacked in Hormuz dead or alive? SC seeks report from government
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has instructed the Union government to look into the baffling case of Capt Ashish Kumar's disappearance. His wife presented a petition with ransom calls and WhatsApp messages hinting at his possible survival. After DNA tests disproved his presumed death following a ship attack, the court is now requesting a status report on the efforts to locate him from the Solicitor General by Monday.

stories.title: Highways may get traffic 'road test' before launch
Trump's voter ID praise follows Gyanesh Kumar - Sergio Gor meet
stories.summary: Recently, US President Donald Trump commended India’s voter ID system after a meeting between Indian election official Gyanesh Kumar and US Ambassador Sergio Gor. Kumar detailed the extensive issuance of photo identity cards and impressive voter turnout in India. He emphasized that the rigorous examination of elections by political parties contributes to high public trust in the electoral process.

Man claims mother-in-law's US visa got 'revoked midflight' for 2-day overstay on previous visit, was sent back from Singapore
BJP puts Vinod Tawde, who played role in Bihar win, in charge of UP
stories.summary: The BJP has designated Vinod Tawde as its new state in-charge for Uttar Pradesh, while Satish Poonia takes the helm in Punjab. Additionally, Tarun Chugh has been entrusted with managing Gujarat's party affairs. These strategic appointments are pivotal as the BJP gears up for the imminent state elections, ensuring that influential leaders are aligned for key electoral battles.

stories.title: British student says he was denied entry to the US despite having valid visa only because he is Muslim: 'Felt as if I was kidnapped'
Goa moves SC, seeks life imprisonment for Tejpal for sex assault
stories.summary: In a significant move, the Goa government has approached the Supreme Court, requesting a harsher sentence for Tarun Tejpal in a sexual assault case. The state argues that his current penalty is insufficient given the severity of the crime. They emphasize that Tejpal exploited his position of power, suggesting that time should not lessen the consequences for such an offense.

Kharge's Vande Mataram dare to BJP: Slap case on Gandhi, Nehru
Chinese doctors claim first-ever successful double thigh replantation; factory worker starts walking again after losing both legs
A San Francisco man was digging in his backyard when his shovel hit something hard
stories.summary: While digging in his San Francisco garden, a gardener stumbled upon an intriguing limestone sculpture. Despite consultations with around fifty experts, its origins remain shrouded in mystery. Given its location near an art school, there may be historical ties to the 1939 Golden Gate International Exposition. The enigmatic bust is set to grace the garden as a captivating centerpiece.

BRICS nations oppose EU carbon border tax at the group's environment ministers’ meeting

stories.title: Indonesian woman gives birth under torchlight during magnitude 7.7 earthquake
Govt announces scheme to incentivise gas companies to expand PNG network
stories.summary: The government has unveiled a dynamic incentive scheme designed to enhance piped gas connections across the nation. By offering distribution companies access to more affordable domestic gas for newly activated connections, the initiative seeks to transform over 50 lakh previously unbilled accounts into operational ones. This strategic move is anticipated to expedite the payback period related to capital investments, encouraging a rapid proliferation of piped cooking gas installations in households.

stories.title: Meet Ohio eighth-grader Archishman Dey who tested 5 household sources; incense produced most PM2.5
stories.summary: Ohio eighth-grader Archishman Dey investigated how everyday household activities affect indoor PM2.5 pollution. Testing an air fryer, candle, humidifier, natural gas and incense, he found incense produced the highest average levels, followed by the air fryer. Inspired by concerns about his grandparents’ asthma, Archishman hopes his findings encourage families to improve indoor air quality.

stories.summary: The Bombay high court (Goa) had recently convicted and sentenced Tejpal to ten years of rigorous imprisonment in the rape case. Tejpal was convicted under Sections 376 (2)(f) (person who is a guardian or in a position of trust or authority rapes a woman), 354-A (sexual harassment) and 354-B (using criminal force on a woman with an intent to disrobe her) of the IPC.

stories.title: NTA removes 600 experts, brings four-tier checks for question papers
AAP leader Satyendar Jain arrested in Delhi Jal Board corruption case
stories.summary: The case includes charges under provisions relating to bribery, criminal breach of trust, cheating and criminal conspiracy. The case was registered on the complaint of Directorate of Vigilance, GNCTD regarding large-scale irregularities, manipulation of tender conditions and criminal conspiracy in the tendering process relating to augmentation/upgradation of Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) of the Delhi Jal Board (DJB).

stories.title: In 1912, a Black couple bought California beachfront land and built a resort; the city seized it and...
stories.summary: In a remarkable turn of events, the Bruce family has regained ownership of their century-old beachfront property, unjustly seized from them in the past. Following this victory, they have transferred it back to Los Angeles County for approximately $20 million. This land, a cherished destination for African Americans during segregation, will now be utilized for lifeguard training facilities.

In 1885, New Zealand introduced hedgehogs to fight pests; today, they threaten native wildlife
stories.summary: European hedgehogs were brought to New Zealand during the 1800s to help manage garden pests. However, these spiky creatures now pose a grave danger to the country's unique wildlife. They feast on the eggs and young of various native species, significantly impacting fragile ecosystems, particularly those involving ground-nesting birds. As a result, ongoing conservation initiatives are prioritizing hedgehog removal to protect these threatened populations.

British Gas customer claimed £300 for solar power but received £38,611.59 by mistake
stories.summary: A British Gas customer experienced an astonishing seven-week ordeal due to a clerical error resulting in a £38,000 overpayment. The lack of clear recovery procedures from customer service compounded the issue. Similarly, another homeowner faced bizarre phantom gas bills lingering for months after the removal of their meter. These situations underscore significant administrative shortcomings within utility firms. After persistent media coverage and follow-ups, both customers received deserved compensation.

stories.title: Who 'killed' Jason Arday? The absurd tragedy of Cambridge's 'youngest black professor'
stories.summary: In every version, Jason Arday the human being disappeared behind Jason Arday the argument” — an examination of who built his myth, benefited from it and vanished when it collapsed.

stories.title: Vijay government to give women employees 365 days maternity leave for third child
stories.summary: Announcing the change in the state assembly during the demand for grants for his department, minister D Sarathkumar said the decision was aimed at strengthening the state's focus on social welfare and women's empowerment. The state had gradually increased maternity leave for its women employees over the years. The original 90-day provision was increased to six months in 2011, followed by an increase to nine months in 2016.

Florida teen Ishanvi Sabniveesu builds AI cane that describes surroundings, works offline and calls for help
stories.summary: Ishanvi Sabniveesu is the innovative mind behind CareCane, an AI-powered cane designed specifically for visually impaired individuals. This remarkable device not only helps users navigate obstacles but also enhances their environmental perception. With offline functionality for broader use and emergency assistance features, CareCane has garnered Sabniveesu second place at the prestigious Invention Convention U.S. Nationals. She is currently focused on introducing additional features and pursuing patent approval.

stories.title: 'Credibility well established globally': MEA on Trump's praise for CEC Gyanesh Kumar
In 1919, German crews sank 52 warships at Scotland's Scapa Flow; decades later...
stories.summary: Following their scuttling in 1919, fifty-two German warships found their final resting place in Scapa Flow. Remarkably, the steel salvaged from these wrecks has been pivotal in numerous modern scientific innovations. This unique pre-nuclear steel has been instrumental in constructing sensitive radiation detectors that safeguard medical imaging and deep-space probes from erroneous readings. To this day, seven of these historic vessels remain preserved for their heritage.

stories.summary: The ambitious dam project planned for the Delaware River faced substantial backlash, resulting in its cancellation. This pivotal decision ultimately fostered the establishment of the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area, a refuge for the river's unspoiled segments. Factors such as environmental concerns and increasing financial burdens were significant in the cancellation, signaling a major milestone in US conservation efforts and land protection strategies.

stories.title: ‘Don’t lie to children’: Rahul slams Rijiju over his 'no one harmed' during CJP stir remark
‘PM CARES? Hardly’: Congress jabs govt for utilising only 0.01% of relief fund
stories.summary: Domestic donations to the PM CARES Fund fell by 30 per cent to nearly Rs 479 crore in the financial year 2024-25, while foreign donations declined by 18 per cent to Rs 92.8 lakh, according to the fund's latest audit report. The total balance in the PM CARES Fund stood at Rs 8,452 crore as on March 31, 2025, compared with Rs 7,173 crore a year earlier.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: Pak SC directs govt to shift Imran to hospital; blast near Kabul school injures around 50 children, and more
stories.summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court ordered the government to move Imran Khan to a hospital for his health. The Supreme Court rejected pleas to replace hanging as the death penalty method. Bihar transferred seventeen senior IPS officers amid controversy over police actions. A hand grenade explosion near a Kabul school injured approximately fifty children. Rishabh Pant became the first Indian to hit one hundred Test sixes.

stories.title: Alaska's live bearcam becomes summer hit as brown bears gather at Brooks Falls to catch salmon
stories.summary: A livestream of brown bears catching sockeye salmon at Brooks Falls in Alaska has attracted 7.3 million views this summer, 70% more than last year. The cameras have built a dedicated fanbase that follows individual bears and tracks their feeding habits. The surge comes as large groups of bears gather at the falls, ahead of Katmai National Park’s annual Fat Bear Week.

stories.title: In 1980, Miles Boekeloo sold his 365-acre retreat, keeping 5 acres and its cabin for 25 years
stories.summary: Miles Boekeloo sold his 365-acre Michigan property to the National Park Service in 1980. His family retained use of five acres and their cabin for 25 years. This allowed them to enjoy their retreat while the land became protected. The property, now Boekelodge, is part of Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore. The cabin and pond remain as traces of the family's connection.

stories.title: Ritabrata Banerjee to remain Bengal LoP till decision on plea within 2 months, says HC
stories.summary: The bench of Justices Shampa Sarkar and Ajay Kumar Gupta directed that the challenge to his appointment be decided by a single judge within two months. The case was filed by Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay, a TMC MLA from the Mamata Banerjee camp, who had challenged assembly speaker Rathindra Bose's decision to appoint Ritabrata Banerjee as the leader of opposition.

stories.title: MGNREGA out, VB-G RAM G in: What changes for rural jobs, workers and states
stories.summary: MGNREGA has been replaced by VB-G RAM G, increasing guaranteed employment days. The new scheme features a revised funding structure and allocation framework for rural India. States will now share program costs with the Centre in a 60:40 ratio. This transition aims to create durable assets and link wage work with village infrastructure. Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra are projected to be significant beneficiaries of this new program.

stories.title: ‘Gandhi, Nehru, Patel sang the same Vande Mataram’: Kharge hits back at BJP amid row
stories.summary: The BJP had criticised the Congress after a video from the party headquarters showed Kharge and Sonia Gandhi speaking while Vande Mataram was being performed during the August 15 Independence Day programme. The BJP accused Congress leadership of disrespecting the national song and sought an apology. The issue remained part of the political discourse in Goa as two stanzas of Vande Mataram were sung in the event attended by Kharge.

stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav is strategically extending his political outreach to Brahmins in preparation for the 2027 elections. He asserts that this community has suffered greatly under the current regime. This initiative seeks to enlarge his political coalition, moving beyond his usual support base. Mayawati rebuts this tactic, labeling it as political trickery. The Brahmin vote is crucial, drawing attention from various political factions.

stories.title: Who was Sonia Bellina? French TikToker‘s burned body found in Saint-Gilles vineyard
stories.summary: French TikToker Sonia Bellina's burned body was recently discovered in a Saint-Gilles vineyard on August 12, 2026. DNA testing reportedly confirmed her identity as French authorities opened an assassination investigation. Investigators are examining the scene and searching for evidence, while unverified online claims about a possible meeting before her disappearance continue circulating. No suspect has been publicly identified in the case so far.

stories.title: Scientists tested two Argentine ant baits; one sent them roaming, other drove them near water
stories.summary: The study from the University of California, Riverside, found that two common ant-bait insecticides can cause very different changes in Argentine ant behaviour before the ants die. Thiamethoxam made affected ants unusually active and sent them roaming outside the nest, while boric acid caused ants to stop foraging and gather inside. The findings show that unusual ant activity after treatment does not necessarily mean the pesticide has failed.

stories.title: Indian-origin mom's $1.7 billion school transportation startup is transforming the lives of American students
stories.summary: Ritu Narayan established Zum to address the challenges parents face in student transportation. The company leverages technology to enhance the school bus experience for children. Zum has now achieved unicorn status with a valuation exceeding one billion dollars and is expanding into the energy market by introducing electric buses. This revolutionary approach is reshaping the way students commute to and from school.

Kick streamer JollyIRL's bungee jump incident in Thailand explained after stream cuts mid-jump
stories.summary: Kick streamer JollyIRL worried viewers after her bungee jump in Pattaya, Thailand, ended with her livestream suddenly cutting off. Fans had no immediate update and some feared she may have been seriously hurt. Sneako also reacted with concern. JollyIRL later confirmed she was okay, while saying her arm and neck hurt and that she believed she had suffered whiplash after the jump.

Canadian mom gets a keyboard tattooed on her arm so her autistic son can ‘talk’
Henrietta Lacks died at 31, but her cells lived on and transformed modern medicine
stories.summary: Henrietta Lacks' cervical cancer cells became immortal, revolutionizing biomedical research and medical advancements. These HeLa cells were vital for developing the polio vaccine and studying various diseases. Her family remained unaware of this scientific breakthrough for decades after her death. The story highlights critical ethical debates concerning patient consent and financial benefits. This legacy continues to shape discussions on scientific progress and human dignity.

Blast near Kabul school injures around 50 children; UN condemns 'heinous' act
In 1999, a Texas couple bought 828 acres and protected 817 for whooping cranes
stories.summary: In Texas, a couple stumbled upon endangered whooping cranes residing on their recently acquired land. Committed to their conservation, they dedicated 817 acres primarily for the cranes' winter haven. The Johnsons' property has transformed into a crucial sanctuary for these magnificent birds, demonstrating the essential role that private lands play in the survival of endangered wildlife.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Kate Middleton: "It is lonely at times and you do feel quite isolated. But actually…"
xQc calls out Hasan for blaming "coordinated smear campaigns" over dog controversy
stories.summary: xQc challenged Hasan Piker to take responsibility for shocking his dog rather than attributing it to smear campaigns. He argued that a simple acknowledgment and apology could have effectively resolved the controversy. Moreover, xQc expressed skepticism about Hasan's choice to hire a dog walker, raising questions about his commitment to his pet's welfare. This debate erupted once again following a viral clip featuring Hasan and his dog, Kaya.

stories.title: In 1989, Apple buried about 2,700 Lisa computers in a landfill; here's why
stories.summary: In 1989, Apple buried about 2,700 unsold Lisa computers at a landfill in Logan, Utah, ending the story of one of its biggest early failures. Launched in 1983 with a graphical interface and mouse, the Lisa was ahead of its time but struggled because of its nearly $10,000 price and hardware problems. A computer reseller later tried to upgrade and sell thousands of the machines, but the effort ultimately failed. Today, surviving Lisa computers are valuable pieces of Apple history.

stories.title: California woman donates $1 million to teachers after learning they were underpaid
Bangladesh does not want Teesta dispute to hurt ties with India, says minister Shahiduddin
stories.summary: The Teesta begins in the Himalayas and flows through Sikkim and West Bengal before entering Bangladesh. It eventually joins the Jamuna, which is the Bangladeshi name for the Brahmaputra. The river is particularly important to northern Bangladesh, where farmers depend on its water. It is also important to West Bengal for irrigation and power generation, with several districts in North Bengal relying on its waters.

stories.title: Ex-Cambridge scholar Nathan Cofnas says he could be murdered after Arday vigil in London
At 75, Jeanne Socrates was badly injured; two years later, she sailed solo around the world at 77
stories.summary: At the inspiring age of 77, British sailor Jeanne Socrates completed a solo, non-stop circumnavigation of the globe. Starting her journey aboard the yacht Nereida from Victoria, Canada, in 2018, she faced tumultuous seas for 320 days. Socrates bravely overcame significant challenges, including repairs and injuries from a serious fall sustained earlier.

stories.title: 'Got trapped in crowd': Bihar govt defends constable who fired AK-47 during students' protests
In 1867, Canterbury released 40 house sparrows to eat pests; 15 years later, they were poisoned
stories.summary: New Zealand introduced house sparrows in 1867 hoping they would help farmers control crop-eating insects. The birds multiplied quickly and soon became a problem, feeding on grains and fruit and damaging wheat, barley and maize crops. Their rapid rise led to organised efforts to control them, including poisoned grain, shooting and bounties for eggs and heads. The story was part of a wider push to introduce European birds for farming and sentimental reasons.

stories.title: 'Tell us our crime': JSSC-CGL exam cancellation ends one protest, sparks another as 2,000 fear job loss
stories.summary: Successful JSSC-CGL candidates protested the Jharkhand government's decision to cancel recruitment exams. They fear losing their government jobs after the cancellation announcement on Monday night. Protesters demanded a CBI probe and an opportunity to defend themselves against allegations. The government defended the cancellation to restore confidence in the recruitment system. Fresh vacancies will provide opportunities for deserving candidates after reforms.

stories.title: Post left Mar-a-Lago to govt hoping it would become 'Winter White House', Trump made her wish true
stories.summary: Mar-a-Lago has a long history that predates Donald Trump and the FBI search. Built in the 1920s by wealthy heiress Marjorie Merriweather Post, the Florida mansion hosted royals, diplomats, lavish parties and charity events. Post later left the estate to the US government as a presidential retreat, but it was eventually bought by Trump in 1985.

‘No state should interfere’: Karnataka CM Shivakumar warns Tamil Nadu over Chamarajanagar killings
stories.summary: Karnataka deputy chief minister warned Tamil Nadu politicians against interference. He asserted Karnataka would protect its territorial sanctity and administration. Tamil Nadu leaders demanded a high-level probe into the August 15 firing incident. Karnataka officials stated forest personnel returned fire in self-defense. The state has ordered a magisterial inquiry and offered interim relief.

stories.title: Indian-origin teen built anti-cyberbullying tech in 2013; now runs non-profit rewarded by Prince Harry and Meghan Markle
stories.summary: Trisha Prabhu created ReThink, a mobile keyboard preventing cyberbullying by prompting users to reconsider offensive messages. This initiative grew into a global non-profit organization supporting millions of students worldwide. Prabhu's work earned her significant recognition and substantial funding for her impactful efforts. She continues to lead ReThink Citizens, promoting digital wellness and a kinder internet. Her dedication exemplifies how one motivated individual can drive significant positive social change.

stories.title: Women were barred from Liechtenstein’s throne for 400 years; new rule lets the firstborn inherit regardless of gender
stories.summary: Liechtenstein has made a progressive move by updating its royal succession laws to favor gender equality. Now, the first-born child will inherit the throne, breaking traditional norms. This decision aligns with several European countries where female heirs are already established, like Great Britain, which pioneered similar reforms in 2011. Meanwhile, Japan still grapples with its frustrating male-only inheritance policy that raises many questions.

stories.title: 'No safe harbour if law violated; message has gone home': Government sources on talks with Meta
stories.summary: India has warned Meta that safe-harbour protection is not guaranteed if laws are violated. Discussions focused on content moderation and child sexual abuse material handling. The government seeks greater local sensitivity in content moderation decisions. Deepfakes and synthetically generated content require clear labeling for users. WhatsApp usernames are also being examined across all messaging platforms.

stories.title: 'Please take Gyanesh Kumar to America': Congress's jibe at CEC after Trump lauds Indian electoral system

Gandhi's letter to India, as told through TOI
stories.summary: From his South Africa years to the freedom struggle, Mahatma Gandhi repeatedly used newspapers to address India’s public. Alok Sharma sifts through letters Gandhi wrote to TOI, illuminating his positions on Satyagraha, the Rowlatt Act, Dalit representation, Hindu-Muslim unity and the hardships faced by Indians in South Africa.

stories.title: In 1964, a Utah businessman built a gas station beside Capitol Reef; after years of conflict...
Karnataka BJP MLA's daughter booked for 'assaulting' woman cop over temple entry queue
stories.summary: During temple festivities, B Suresh Gowda's daughter, a Karnataka BJP MLA, was accused of assaulting a woman police sub-inspector. The altercation began over access to the queue, leading to allegations of abuse and physical confrontation by the officer. In response, the MLA's daughter filed a counter-complaint currently under investigation. The MLA expressed regret for the incident and emphasized the need for appropriate legal action.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: Delhi HC gets bomb threat; US loses 45 Reaper drones in Iran war, & more
stories.summary: A bomb threat email targeted the Delhi High Court ahead of Independence Day celebrations. Reports indicate the US military lost forty-five Reaper drones in its conflict with Iran. The Supreme Court disapproved of the Bar Council of India's action against NALSAR students. Congress questioned the Centre's approach to the caste census format. Former Manchester United and Aston Villa goalkeeper Jimmy Rimmer has died at seventy-eight.

stories.title: Pakistani minister in Balochistan province escapes armed attack on convoy
stories.summary: .The attack took place in the Khad Kocha area as Langove was travelling from Quetta to Kalat, Balochistan government spokesperson Shahid Rind said. "Six people were injured in the attack, but the minister remained unhurt and the convoy has returned to Quetta," Rind said. All six injured people suffered bullet wounds, according to a senior police official. Three of them were police personnel, with two reportedly in serious condition.

stories.title: London river was declared 'biologically dead' in 1957; decades later it is filled with sharks and seals
stories.summary: The River Thames in London has made a remarkable recovery, evolving from a biologically barren stretch to a vibrant ecosystem full of life, such as sharks and seals. This revitalization is attributed to decades of pollution management and enhanced sewage systems. The Thames Tideway Tunnel plays a crucial role in minimizing sewage discharge. However, challenges like warming waters and nitrate pollution still pose threats.

stories.title: UK heatwaves help bananas fruit, experts explain why it’s unusual
Ryanair passenger partially sucked through airplane window after engine blade smashed into cabin: Report
GOBARdhan scheme: How India plans to turn cattle dung, crop waste and garbage into fuel
stories.summary: India's GOBARdhan scheme targets ten-fold growth in compressed biogas production. This initiative aims to convert agricultural residue and cattle dung into valuable fuel. The government provides capital assistance and assured demand for producers. This framework seeks to build a national bioenergy industry from organic waste. The scheme intends to enhance energy security and rural development.

stories.title: Nigel Farage beats ‘space warrior trashcan’ rival in UK by-poll he triggered
stories.summary: Nigel Farage claimed a decisive win in the Clacton parliamentary by-election, following his resignation amid controversies surrounding his financial dealings. His nearest rival, the comedic character Count Binface, surprisingly garnered a considerable share of support. Meanwhile, prominent parties in Westminster chose to abstain from the election, deeming it a mere political ploy. This by-election stemmed from Farage's prior resignation and his ambition to retake his seat.

stories.title: Bernie Marcus' foundation gives $28.7M for heart-repair stem cell research
7,000-year-old ‘Stargazer’ statuette from ancient Turkey raises mysteries
stories.summary: A 5,000-year-old marble statuette called "The Stargazer" originates from ancient Turkey. This rare figure, dating to 3000 BCE, is remarkably whole and unbroken. Its oversized head and upward gaze create a distinctive, stylized human form. The statuette's original purpose remains a mystery due to its ancient origins. Similar figures have been found across Western Anatolia and nearby regions.

stories.title: 'Not said, but presented as if it was': CJI Surya Kant says 'cockroach' remark 'misquoted'
Quote of the day by Martin Luther King Jr: 'There is some good in the worst of us and some evil in the best of us. When we discover this, we are less prone to hate our enemies'
stories.summary: Martin Luther King Jr. eloquently illustrates the dual nature of humanity and our collective imperfections. By acknowledging our flaws, we foster empathy, which diminishes hostility and paves the way for productive conflict resolution. This understanding of shared vulnerabilities encourages dialogue and reconciliation, transforming resentment into compassion and commitment to understanding one another.

stories.title: Massachusetts residents sue data centre over 27 diesel generators near homes
Volhynia massacres: Russia using WWII to plant discord between Ukraine and Poland?
stories.summary: The historical dispute centres on the Volhynia massacres between 1943 and 1945. Poland says Ukrainian nationalists killed around 100,000 Poles during the violence, while thousands of Ukrainians were also killed in retaliatory attacks. Tensions over the issue increased after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy named an army unit after insurgents linked to the massacres. Polish president Karol Nawrocki responded by stripping Zelenskyy of a major Polish honour in June.

stories.title: Why has Britain's grass turned yellow? Scientists warn about the future of the island after 'driest month ever'
stories.summary: After experiencing the driest July on record, England's picturesque green fields have succumbed to a fading yellow hue. This alarming trend of increasing heatwaves significantly affects lawns and public parks. While native grasses possess resilience during droughts and can deepen their roots to conserve water, extended dry periods inevitably lead them to enter a dormant state, awaiting rain.

stories.title: Nearly 80 men found shackled in an ancient Athens mass grave were locals
18-year-old turns back 400m from Everest summit, returns a year later to make history
‘Congress responsible for Partition’: CM Yogi says India would be different if Modi were PM in 1947
stories.summary: Speaking at an event in Lucknow marking Partition Horrors Remembrance Day, CM Yogi said the Congress had failed the country by prioritising political power and alleged that the consequences of Partition continue to affect India. “Had Narendra Modi been the Prime Minister of India at the time of Independence, nobody would have been able to damage India in the slightest,” he said.

stories.title: 'First time we did something like this': Former women Naxalites share their Raipur ramp-walk experience
stories.summary: The women, all from Sukma, took part in a Swadeshi fashion show organised as part of rehabilitation efforts for former Naxalites. Sukma SP Mayank Gurjar said the event also gave them an opportunity to promote Swadeshi products. For some of the women, the experience was unlike anything they had done before. One former Naxalite said she surrendered in 2026 and travelled to Raipur for six days of training.

stories.title: Surrogacy dispute escalates after McKenna West gives birth to baby with heart defect
stories.summary: The surrogacy dispute escalated significantly when McKenna West delivered a newborn with a critical heart condition. This infant is currently under the care of intended parents Nausheen Gilkar and Omar Ahmed. Meanwhile, West is fighting against the custody agreements and claims over parental rights in Texas, where the intricate web of contrasting state laws complicates the situation, leading to ongoing legal battles as all parties await further judicial rulings.

stories.title: RG Kar victim's 'hurried' cremation: Mob attacks arrested ex-TMC MLA with footwear, eggs, muck; video
'Serious doubts on intent': Congress attacks Centre over caste census format; cites Telangana model
Australia’s feral camels roamed free for decades. Now Gulf breeders want them
Quote of the day by MacKenzie Scott: "People struggling against inequities deserve center stage in…"
Beluga whales may recognise themselves after 98-session study
Colorado’s 2024 restoration efforts for Preble’s mouse gain momentum with new habitat project
stories.summary: Colorado is taking significant steps to ensure the survival of the endangered Preble's meadow jumping mouse. Efforts focus on restoring essential streamside ecosystems and linking them to floodplains. Landowners are invited to join this initiative through voluntary conservation measures and financial support. A conservation bank was established in 2024 to facilitate these vital restoration projects, with new initiatives rolling out in 2026 to enhance habitat safeguarding.

stories.title: 'Astronauts' land on road craters: Over 100 Jaipur residents stage unique protest against potholes
stories.summary: Gokulpura residents staged a protest on Pratap Circle Road, highlighting poor road conditions. Two individuals dressed as astronauts entered water-filled potholes, simulating a lunar landscape. This unusual demonstration aimed to draw attention to neglected infrastructure and drainage issues. Residents have sought attention from local officials for several months regarding these problems. Tenders for road and drainage work have been awarded and will commence after the monsoon.

stories.title: Iran president Pezeshkian to visit India for BRICS summit amid Middle East tensions
stories.summary: Iran has signalled that it sees India as a potential partner in efforts to ease tensions in West Asia, with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying New Delhi could play a greater role in de-escalating the ongoing crisis. Araghchi made the remarks during his visit to India in June. He said Tehran did not see a military solution to the conflict and believed that negotiations offered only viable way forward.

stories.title: BCI action, U-turn and SC rebuke: How NALSAR students' protest against CJI kicked up a row
Wyoming fossils reveal ancient forests collapsed after extreme global warming
SC quashes all FIRs against Samay Raina, Ranveer Allahabadia in ‘India’s Got Latent’ case
stories.summary: Along with Raina, the court quashed the FIRs and related proceedings against comedians Vipul Goyal, Balraj Paramjeet Singh Ghai, Sonali Thakkar and Nishant Jagdish Tanwar. The proceedings stemmed from jokes made by the five, which were flagged by the M/s SMA Cure Foundation, an organisation working with people affected by Spinal Muscular Atrophy and other rare diseases.

stories.title: Indian-origin man rejected for H-1B three times, spent $13,000 and formed 700 pages of evidence to stay in US
stories.summary: Sohan Sethi faced multiple H-1B visa rejections after arriving in the United States. He then pursued an O-1 visa, requiring extensive documentation and lawyer fees. Sethi demonstrated extraordinary ability through achievements and industry recognition to secure his stay. This path highlights the challenges faced by skilled professionals seeking to remain in America. He now manages a team, sharing his experience to guide others through the process.

stories.title: Great Barrier Reef coral cover rebounds to 35.1% despite bleaching
‘I am not scared’: Sukhbir Singh Badal after discharge from hospital day after attack in Nanded
Shakespeare's birth home was nearly shipped to US in 1847; it was saved from a showman's fantasy with a payment of £3,000
stories.summary: In the 1840s, Shakespeare's birthplace in Stratford-upon-Avon faced the threat of sale, as American showman P.T. Barnum aimed to move the historic home to New York. A dedicated committee formed, rallying public donations and support from notable figures like Prince Albert to save the site. Their efforts culminated in the successful acquisition of the house at auction in 1847, ensuring the preservation of this cherished cultural landmark.

stories.title: Egyptian archaeologists uncover 3 tombs, 5 mummies, and Roman remains
stories.summary: An Egyptian archaeological mission has uncovered three tombs at the Sheikh Sobi site. These burials include mummies and sarcophagi from the Late and Roman periods. One tomb contained five mummies, dating to the Late Period. The other two tombs are believed to be from the Roman period. These discoveries offer insights into the Bahariya Oasis's ancient communities.

stories.title: Delhi High Court, IGI airport, 3 govt offices get bomb threats ahead of Independence Day
Ohio family restores 60 acres of abandoned mine land with native trees
Morocco is testing a 'sponge' pavement that stays 16°F cooler by itself, aims at replacing black asphalt
stories.summary: Morocco is pioneering a novel sponge pavement designed to enhance water management and mitigate heat effects. Unlike conventional black asphalt, this innovative surface enables water to seep through, promoting natural cooling through evaporation when moisture exists. This initiative aims to bolster urban climate resilience and elevate the comfort of residents, with pilot projects underway in Marrakech and Agadir as part of a larger sustainable city initiative.

stories.title: Iowa man faces 124 charges after alleged capture of rare Alabama turtle
Savarkar defamation case: Supreme Court quashes Lucknow Court order summoning Rahul Gandhi
'Our red line': Shehbaz Sharif threatens India with 'direct response' over Indus Water Treaty
Couple renovating their farmhouse kitchen found more than 1,000 coins buried
Union minister JP Nadda admitted to AIIMS Delhi after uneasiness
North Carolina woman survived 14,500-foot fall and 200+ fire-ant stings
Thousands of tiny earthquakes went unnoticed beneath Alaska for years
'China stopped our army from patrolling several places in Arunachal': Rahul Gandhi slams Centre
Quote of the day by Paul Walker: "If you play with people who are better than you, then…"
‘Shouldn’t govt give employment?’ Supreme Court stays HC order on jobs for Karur stampede victims' kin
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has stayed a Madras High Court order regarding government jobs. This order had previously struck down the Tamil Nadu government's decision for stampede victims' relatives. The Supreme Court questioned the challenge to the government's policy for affected families. The High Court had quashed appointments, citing existing guidelines and potential demands. The Supreme Court's stay provides interim relief to the Tamil Nadu government.

stories.title: Bill Ackman’s road to billions began with $14,000 and a Buffett-linked book
Colorado mom gets her son ‘arrested’ after he refuses to take a first-day-of-school photo
80th Independence Day: 1,057 police, fire and correctional personnel receive gallantry, service medals
stories.summary: Over one thousand personnel received Gallantry and Service Medals this Independence Day. Gallantry Medals recognized exceptional courage and actions in critical situations. Many gallantry awards went to personnel serving in Left Wing Extremism-affected areas. President's Medals for Distinguished Service honored special records in their respective fields. Meritorious Service Medals acknowledged valuable service marked by devotion to duty.

stories.title: 'No inquiry': Bar Council of India's U-turn on order against law students over CJI visit
German startup Voodin swaps fibreglass for wood turbine blades, aiming for recyclable blades at commercial scale
stories.summary: A pioneering startup in Germany is crafting wind turbine blades using laminated veneer lumber, presenting a sustainable solution to the prevalent fiberglass composite problem. The initial prototypes are currently being tested in the field, demonstrating their potential. This innovation seeks to tackle the increasing challenge of waste generated by conventional wind turbine blades, with plans for larger models aimed at commercial projects on the horizon.

stories.title: 'Uncalled for': CJI pulls up Bar Council of India over threat of action against NALSAR students
Six generations return to Lake Winnipesaukee for a century-old tradition
After 14 years, Massachusetts dam removal begins to restore 7 miles of stream
Hours into probe, police yet to find motive behind Sukhbir Badal's attack
Harsimrat Kaur Badal 'deeply touched' by PM Modi's 'kind gesture' after attack on Sukhbir Badal
Bangladesh PM likely to visit India as Dhaka presses for Sheikh Hasina's extradition
'A moment that tore apart several lives': PM Modi on Partition Horrors Remembrance Day
Rebel TMC group leader Sudip urges PM Modi to appoint NDA convener
stories.summary: In an effort to enhance communication, a leader from the Trinamool Congress has urged Prime Minister Modi to appoint an NDA convener. This request coincides with their faction's push for a merger with another party, seeking clarity on their legitimacy within the alliance. Additionally, the party plans to approach the Supreme Court regarding disqualification issues with rebel Lok Sabha members, aiming for a swift resolution.

TMC gears up to move Supreme Court within 10 days to seek disqualification of 20 rebel MPs
Kharge claims stage 'purified' after his speech in Haldwani, govt promises action
Mines, minerals bill gets nod, draws fire from Jharkhand, Kerala
Opposition claims grand success, says it forced goverment to put off 5 bills
Paranormal Creator’s Fatal Crash: Jiang Xiaorou dies after July accident; family urges fans to stop speculation
stories.summary: Jiang Xiaorou, a 24-year-old Chinese paranormal content creator, died on August 10 after suffering severe injuries in a July 15 traffic accident. Known for challenging superstition, she had more than 1.28 million Douyin followers. Her controversial videos, including one showing her destroying a Guanyin statue, resurfaced after her death. However, there is no evidence linking her accident to supernatural punishment, despite speculation circulating online.

stories.title: Over 11k Indian workers died in Saudi, UAE each in 2021-25, MEA informs Parliament
Rahul Gandhi appears like a failed comedian: BJP
SC tells UPSC to defer call on Odisha DGP pick
Air India begins dope test on all its 5,000 pilots
Phuket plunge: Airbus sends initial report to AI, seeks maintenance details
BCI bars Nalsar students over CJI Surya Kant protest, retracts
Owens Reframes Kirk Assassination: Owens says grief fuels spiritual mission; video blends faith and audience engagement
stories.summary: Candace Owens has opened up about how her feelings changed following Charlie Kirk’s assassination. She said she has moved beyond the initial trauma and no longer feels haunted, instead believing Kirk is spiritually “fighting alongside” her. Owens connected her optimism to her belief that truth will prevail and said she feels Charlie is still with them. She also encouraged viewers to support her show by purchasing merchandise.

stories.title: Amazon AI Opt-Out Backlash: Twitch auto-enables training on streams; creators must change privacy settings
stories.summary: Twitch is facing criticism over a new setting that allows Amazon to use streamer content for generative AI training by default. Streamers can opt out through their privacy settings. Users questioned why the option was not turned off unless creators agreed. Twitch said it is not training GenAI models itself, but the setting covers Amazon’s AI model training.

US saw most cases of attack on Indians abroad in 2021-25: MEA
Disproportionate assets case: Rahul Gandhi questions Allahabad HC order, says shift case
SC slams Centre &FSSAI, says you can’t take court for a ride
Consumer forums can’t be mere rehabalitaion centres for retired: Supreme Court
Quote by Karl Popper: 'Those who promise us paradise on earth never produced anything but a hell'
stories.summary: Karl Popper highlighted the dangers of striving for a perfect society, warning that such aspirations frequently lead to disastrous outcomes. He pointed out how leaders driven by utopian dreams tend to accumulate excessive power, often resulting in brutality. The French Revolution and several authoritarian regimes serve as stark illustrations of this trend. In the current era, technological advancements and corporate ideologies can echo these same pitfalls.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Zeno: 'We have two ears and one mouth, so we should listen more than we say'
stories.summary: Zeno of Citium, originally a Phoenician trader, established Stoicism in the heart of ancient Athens. He advocated that true listening is an intentional skill rather than simply a precursor to responding. This timeless philosophy champions the value of understanding prior to action. Contemporary studies validate that active listening boosts trust and mitigates conflict, emphasizing the age-old design of our auditory and vocal apparatus.

stories.title: ‘We can drive them crazy’: Rahul Gandhi takes aim at PM Modi, Amit Shah
1991 Jammu Tawi railway station blast: GRP nets fugitive terrorist after 35 year run
Farooq doubts terror threat to Kashmiri Pandits, seeks probe
Quote of the day by CT Fletcher: "Everything is impossible, until someone crazy enough comes along and…"
In 1962, New Jersey took a family's property; they challenged the price and were awarded $350,000
stories.summary: Exploring vintage postcards reveals a fascinating glimpse into coastal life in early New Jersey. Historian John Joseph Patrick Mulhern recounted his experiences on Sandy Hook, describing the thrilling days of tracking ships and conducting groundbreaking radio experiments. He vividly portrayed the operations of the Navesink lighthouses and the evolving landscape, showcasing the rich maritime heritage and community growth of the time.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Cristiano Ronaldo: "I don't mind people hating me, because…"
'Soon in a trash can': Iran mocks Trump's secret getaway via catering truck
Mohuya Khan made about $130,000 from nine income streams while living in Queens, after taxes she...
stories.summary: Mohuya Khan, a dynamic 27-year-old content creator, skillfully juggled nine diverse income streams from her cozy one-bedroom apartment in Astoria, Queens. Her hard work paved the way to financial independence, allowing her to eliminate debts. Yet, the toll of her bustling schedule led to considerable burnout. Recognizing this, Khan has now implemented healthier boundaries to prioritize her overall well-being.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Dale Carnegie: "When we have accepted the worst, we have nothing more to lose. And that automatically means…"
James, 18, Earl of Wessex, passes A-levels, to study at Royal Agricultural University
stories.summary: James, 18, Earl of Wessex, has passed his A-levels and will study rural land management at the Royal Agricultural University in Gloucestershire. Prince Edward and Sophie’s son spent part of the summer working as a farmhand at King Charles III’s Sandringham estate, where he was reportedly seen driving tractors and embracing hands-on work.

stories.title: Passenger train derails, flips on side near UK's Lewes; rail routes disrupted
Delhi govt notifies 20% horizontal quota for ex-Agniveers in prison department jobs
She spent 10 months restoring a 160-year-old house; now Lauren Iraeta is reconnecting families...
stories.summary: Lauren Iraeta approached her home renovation as a journey through time, merging creativity with historical inquiry. By delving into neglected family records and tales from earlier occupants, she uncovered names etched within the widow's walk. This captivating endeavor brought descendants closer to their ancestors' cherished childhood narratives, illuminating the profound history woven into these aged abodes.

stories.title: CAG finds 98% shortfall in Green India Mission forest cover targets, red-flags multiple lapses
stories.summary: The Comptroller and Auditor General raised concerns about the inadequacies within the Green India Mission program, noting that the goal of increasing forest cover was far from realized over a decade. The audit pointed to significant issues in planning and financial oversight, which severely undermined the mission's objectives. Key vulnerable areas were neglected during afforestation, diminishing efforts to combat climate change.

stories.title: In June 2026, Washington began restoring 270 acres across two river islands; the project will...
stories.summary: In June 2026, heavy machinery commenced work on a significant coastal restoration initiative. The plan involves the dismantling of outdated sea defenses and the breaching of river levees on two islands, aiming to transform 270 acres of previously cultivated land into natural intertidal wetlands. This restoration will create critical habitats for juvenile Puget Sound Chinook salmon, with the completion date set for autumn 2028.

stories.title: 'Majority of students innocent': BCI reverses ban on NALSAR 2026 batch over CJI invite row
stories.summary: The Bar Council of India has revised its previous directive concerning NALSAR graduates. Students from NALSAR's 2026 cohort can now pursue enrollment with state bar councils. This update followed significant backlash against the original ruling, which prevented these students from becoming advocates due to their association with a protest. The regulator emphasized that the majority of the students were uninvolved and innocent.

stories.title: Danube River reveals Nazi warships hidden underwater for 80 years
‘Since it’s written, it has to be done’: Law minister's delimitation push comes with Constitution jibe at Opp
Who is Yalda Moaiery? Iranian photojournalist sentenced to 15 years over images, reporting
Meet Jimmy Chilimigras, the Mississippi teen who finished high school at 12
stories.summary: At just 18 years old, James Chilimigras has achieved remarkable academic milestones, having graduated from Loyola University New Orleans College of Law, where he ranked in the top two percent of his class while earning five certificates. Displaying an exceptional intellect, he completed both his bachelor's and master’s degrees by the age of 15 and became the youngest Certified Public Accountant in history.

stories.title: 'No clear information': Nepal ‘loses’ papers of centuries-old treaty defining borders with India
stories.summary: Nepal's foreign minister announced that the country might have misplaced the original Sugauli Treaty papers, which played a critical role in establishing its borders with British India after the Anglo-Nepalese War. This comes at a time when border disputes with India have intensified. The government plans to systematically assess numerous international agreements, seeking to amend or renew any that are no longer pertinent.

stories.title: North America’s longest cable-stayed bridge is now open with a massive 853-metre crossing
Meet Scarlett Tiani, the Connecticut student whose dog-safety invention reached US Nationals
stories.summary: In a remarkable achievement, Connecticut student Scarlett Tiani has garnered national attention for her inventive pet safety solution, Tail Wag Warning. Designed to enhance safety during unexpected dog interactions, Tiani's creation received numerous accolades at the prestigious national Invention Convention. With legal support at her side, she is now set to embark on the journey of securing a U.S. patent for her groundbreaking invention.

stories.title: 2027 UP assembly elections: How parties are vying for Dalit votes amid Mayawati’s shrinking base
stories.summary: A notable evolution in Dalit politics is unfolding in Uttar Pradesh, marked by a decline in the Bahujan Samaj Party's dominance. The Bharatiya Janata Party and the Samajwadi Party are actively courting Dalit voters ahead of elections, and the Congress party is also working to regain its historic connections. Meanwhile, Chandrashekhar Azad is establishing a distinct political identity, foreshadowing a significant shift in the Dalit electoral landscape.

stories.title: 'No NALSAR 2026 graduate will be enrolled as advocate': BCI amid CJI convocation invite row
stories.summary: The Bar Council of India has put a pause on NALSAR's enrollments for the 2026 law graduates. This decision comes in the wake of an alleged smear campaign against Chief Justice Surya Kant's presence at the convocation. The Council demands a comprehensive report from NALSAR within three days, requiring identification of those behind this campaign. The situation will be reviewed on August 19, 2026.

stories.title: Elizabeth Hird bought Outer Island in 1964; in 1995, she donated it for wildlife, research and education
stories.summary: Outer Island, once a charming summer getaway, has been transformed into a vital protected wildlife refuge. The island was generously donated to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service by Elizabeth Hird in 1995, with the intention of preserving its natural resources and fostering education and research. Today, it serves as an invaluable living laboratory for students and researchers alike, ensuring a sustainable conservation legacy for generations to come.

stories.title: New Jersey begins restoration work to bring back forest and wetland habitat along Raritan river
stories.summary: A 112-acre restoration project has begun along New Jersey's Raritan River to restore floodplain forest, wetlands and wildlife habitat affected by past contamination linked to the American Cyanamid Superfund Site. The project will plant about 50,000 native trees and shrubs, create three acres of vernal pools, control invasive plants and protect new vegetation with deer fencing. The restored site will be monitored and managed for 15 years.

stories.title: Michigan's historic Ford House is replacing concrete shoreline with natural habitat
stories.summary: A groundbreaking initiative along Michigan's Lake St. Clair is reshaping the shoreline into thriving natural wetlands. By dismantling decades of concrete barriers, this project endeavors to create essential habitats for local fish populations. The transformation revolves around the historic Edsel and Eleanor Ford Estate, aiming to revitalize coastal marshes while boosting biodiversity and community education on ecosystem preservation.

stories.title: Engulfed in flames, smoke: 2 killed as Russia hits passenger train with 340 onboard, says Zelenskyy
stories.summary: A Ukrainian passenger train in the Odesa region fell victim to a Russian drone strike, leading to the unfortunate demise of the driver and assistant. Simultaneously, Ukrainian military forces conducted a successful operation against a large oil refinery in Bashkortostan, causing extensive fire damage. This series of events serves as a stark reminder of the ongoing hostilities plaguing the region.

stories.title: US sex trafficking prosecutions drop 22% amid Trump immigration crackdown: Report
Parle retains India's most chosen in-home FMCG crown for 14th consecutive year
Washington man accused of shooting bald eagle found near his chickens now faces federal charges
From erotic fantasy to Indian identity, a famous Italian calendar finds a new story
stories.summary: The 2027 edition of the Pirelli Calendar pays homage to India, showcasing a stunning lineup of local talent. Initiated by renowned Norwegian photographer Sølve Sundsbø alongside the late Raghu Rai, the project has been lovingly completed by his daughter Avani Rai. This iteration embraces outdoor settings, featuring both celebrated icons and skilled local artisans, reflecting a profound evolution from sensual imagery to the celebration of cultural identity and diverse narratives.

stories.title: 'Purify your own minds': SP’s Akhilesh hits out at BJP over 'suddhikaran' at Kharge rally venue
Meet Stephen Jalland: 57-year-old English handyman clearing gardens for free
Real 'Sena' battle: 'Sin' of defection should not be rewarded, Uddhav camp tells SC
stories.summary: Uddhav Thackeray's Shiv Sena faction argued in the Supreme Court today. They stated constitutional provisions should not encourage anti-defection law violations. The court heard arguments on the party symbol dispute and faction recognition. Arguments focused on distinguishing splits from disqualification proceedings. The hearing continues on August 18, with the court considering the nature of a party split.

stories.title: 'PM Modi does not sleep at night, Shah disappeared': Rahul mocks BJP, says India expressing itself
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi firmly asserted that the Congress party's primary function is to enhance the expression of India’s citizens. He articulated concerns about the government's tendencies to silence dissent and manipulate information. Furthermore, Gandhi lambasted the government’s foreign policy strategies and the failure of the RSS to comprehend the complexities of contemporary Indian society.

stories.title: Trump admin urges Supreme Court to lift block on mail-voting order ahead of midterms election
Evening news wrap: Sukhbir Badal attacked in Nanded; Air India begins pilot drug testing, & more
stories.summary: Sukhbir Singh Badal faced a kirpan attack at a Nanded gurdwara, while a police inspector was injured. Air India has initiated mandatory substance screening for all its pilots following a recent incident. Ukraine's President Zelenskyy is requesting more Patriot missiles from the United States. The Indian Air Force is moving forward with a large transport aircraft acquisition deal.

stories.title: 'Modi thinks foreign policy is this': Rahul mocks PM; another Congress leader takes Meloni swipe
Bengal govt strips BJP MP Ananta Maharaj of Banga Bibhushan award over 'insulting' remarks against Netaji
stories.summary: In a significant move, the West Bengal government has rescinded the Banga Bibhushan award granted to Ananta Maharaj. This decision arose from his controversial comments questioning Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose’s leadership and the establishment of the Azad Hind Fauj. The remarks have sparked strong backlash from various political factions and groups, underscoring the deep emotions tied to the legacy of this revered freedom fighter.

stories.title: Carmela Chillery-Watson became the youngest MBE recipient after raising funds for muscular dystrophy
stories.summary: Carmela Chillery-Watson became the youngest MBE recipient at eleven years old. She received the honour for her extensive fundraising and awareness work. This recognition celebrated her dedication to Muscular Dystrophy UK and the disabled community. Carmela's journey began after her diagnosis with a rare muscle-wasting condition at age four. Her continued advocacy aims to promote accessibility and support for those affected.

stories.title: In 2022, Buffalo completed the first emerald shiner passage on the Niagara River; four years later...
stories.summary: The city of Buffalo is enhancing a fish passageway to facilitate the journey of emerald shiners to Lake Erie. By installing steel baffles along the seawall, this initiative aims to mitigate strong currents. This effort is part of a significant multi-million-dollar restoration project for the Niagara River Area, alongside transforming nearby industrial slips into crucial shallow-water habitats, all geared towards rectifying historic environmental harm in western New York.

stories.title: 'This is your last chance': SC ultimatum to Centre over delay in front-of-pack food warning labels
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has expressed strong disapproval towards the government's procrastination regarding food warning labels, specifically calling out the FSSAI. The justices mandated that the Centre has a fortnight to cement its decision, prioritizing public health, particularly for children. The court dismissed claims surrounding traditional foods and foreign standards, signaling that judicial actions could follow if a definitive choice remains absent.

stories.title: How silver made Calico a 3,000-person boomtown before it became a ghost town
Amondawa tribe does not use weeks, months or years to describe time
stories.summary: The Amondawa tribe structures their daily living around significant events and life phases rather than fixed numbers of weeks or years. Their language features an absence of abstract units of time, showcasing a unique relationship between age and identity rooted in transitional life stages. This inquiry prompts a reevaluation of conventional beliefs regarding human perceptions of time.

stories.title: Washington launches project to restore 270 acres of Skagit estuary habitat
stories.summary: In a significant environmental effort, the restoration of 270 acres of estuary habitat in the South Fork Skagit River is underway, starting from June 2026 and set to finish by fall 2028. This initiative focuses on enhancing the habitat for the endangered Puget Sound Chinook salmon, ensuring a sustainable ecosystem by reconnecting islands to tidal flows, and supporting various wildlife, including waterfowl and shorebirds.

stories.title: 70 million years ago, Earth had 372 days a year, with days lasting 23 hours
stories.summary: Research into ancient shells has unveiled that Earth experienced a 372-day year around seventy million years ago. During the Cretaceous period, each day was approximately twenty-three hours and thirty-one minutes long. This study also examined the ancient Earth-Moon distance and revealed warmer ocean temperatures, with evidence of photosymbiosis. The mollusc fossil indicates it thrived for over nine years on a tropical seabed.

Why are streamers calling out Twitch after ExtraEmily is named Ambassador despite backlash?
stories.summary: Twitch has sparked controversy by appointing ExtraEmily as a new Ambassador despite her history of unsafe driving during streams, leading to multiple suspensions. A particularly alarming incident involved her nearly colliding with another vehicle while live. This choice has prompted critics to question Twitch's commitment to its community guidelines, with many feeling that it sends a troubling message about safety and accountability.

stories.title: SAD chief Sukhbir Badal attacked: 62-year-old assailant had been working at Nanded gurdwara for 2 years as 'sevadar'
stories.summary: Sukhbir Singh Badal faced an unsettling attack during his visit to Mata Sahib Gurdwara in Nanded, Maharashtra, where an assailant attempted to stab him. Fortunately, security personnel quickly intervened to subdue the attacker, who had been living at the gurdwara for two years. Badal suffered a hand injury and received necessary medical care, while a security inspector was also injured.

stories.title: Romania has declared a 30-day energy alert as Danube river levels fall too low to cool its nuclear reactors
stories.summary: In response to alarming low levels of the Danube river, Romania's energy sector is on high alert. Unit one of the Cernavoda nuclear power facility has ceased operations due to water scarcity. To maintain unit two's functionality, emergency measures including river dredging have been implemented. Authorities have also undertaken the blasting of rock formations to facilitate better water flow. Residents are urged to conserve electricity during high-demand evenings.

Rising temperatures are transforming Ireland into a rare wine country; the island now has 42 vineyards with upcoming bumper crops
stories.summary: As climate change enhances grape-growing conditions, Irish winemakers foresee a bountiful harvest. Expanding vineyards are drawing considerable attention from international investors. The unique interplay of soil and coastal weather is enabling the production of exquisite wines. To adapt to Ireland's cooler climate, new grape varieties are being introduced, with a focus on high-quality output to ensure competitiveness on the global stage.
